What is the ratio of SI earned on a sum at 21% for 8 yr to that earned on same sum at same rate for 21 yr?
A person took a loan of ₹ 1200 on simple interest for as many years as the rate of interest. If interest paid is ₹ 432, find the rate.
A sum amounts to ₹ 1725 in 3 yr and ₹ 1875 in 5 yr at simple interest. The rate is:
explain: SI for 2 yr $= 150 \Rightarrow$ SI for 1 yr $= 75$. Principal $= 1725 - 225 = 1500$. $R = \frac{75 \times 100}{1500} = 5\%$.

q: If the simple interest for 8 yr is equal to 40% of the principal, then after how many years will it be equal to the principal?
explain: 40% interest in 8 yr $\Rightarrow R = 40/8 = 5\%$. For $SI = P$ (100% interest), $T = 100/5 = 20 \text{ yr}$.

q: Find the simple interest on ₹ 3200 at 4.5% p.a. for 2 yr 9 months.
A sum at 7.5% p.a. amounts to ₹ 11025 after 3 yr. What is the simple interest?
Amount payable after 5.5 yr on ₹ 4750 was ₹ 6840. Find the rate of interest.
A sum of money at simple interest doubles in 7 yr. It will become four times in:
explain: Double ($SI=P$) in 7 yr. Four times ($SI=3P$) takes $3 \times 7 = 21 \text{ yr}$.

q: A sum invested at SI becomes 3 times itself in 25 yr. How many times will it become in 75 yr?
explain: 3 times ($SI=2P$) in 25 yr. In 75 yr, $SI = 2P \times 3 = 6P$. Amount $= P + 6P = 7P$.

q: An amount becomes double in 7 yr on simple interest. The amount would be four times in how many years?
explain: $SI=P$ in 7 yr. For 4 times ($SI=3P$), time $= 3 \times 7 = 21 \text{ yr}$.

q: A sum was invested for 2 yr. Had rate been 3% higher, interest would be ₹ 240 more. Find sum.
₹ 800 becomes ₹ 920 in 3 yr at SI. If rate is increased by 4%, find the new amount.
Amount after 1 yr was ₹ 1484. If rate was 2% higher, amount would be ₹ 26.50 more. Find original interest.
explain: Extra interest $26.50 = P \times 0.02 \times 1 \Rightarrow P = 1325$. Original SI $= 1484 - 1325 = ₹ 159$.

q: Sum invested at r% for 3 yr. If rate was (r+2)%, interest would be ₹ 84 more. Find sum.
Difference of SI on ₹ 8000 in 3 yr from two banks is ₹ 800. Find difference in rates.
Sum of ₹ 5000 for 10 yr: 6% for first 2 yr, 8% for next 2 yr, 10% beyond. Find total interest.
SI on sum for 15 months at 7.5% exceeds SI for 8 months at 12.5% by ₹ 32.50. Find sum.
Borrows ₹ 5000 at 4% p.a. for 2 yr and lends it at 6.25% p.a. for 2 yr. Find gain.
SI for 4.4 yr at 9.5% is ₹ 3553. Find amount at 8.4% for 7.5 yr on same sum.
Bhawna borrowed ₹ 4500 from a lender at the rate of 15% per annum, simple interest on 26 March, 2018 and cleared the loan on 7 June of the same year. What amount did she pay to clear her loan?
explain: Number of days: March (5) + April (30) + May (31) + June (7) = 73 days. $SI = \frac{4500 \times 15 \times 73}{100 \times 365} = ₹ 135$. Amount $= 4500 + 135 = ₹ 4635$.

q: A sum of ₹ 5000 was lent partly at 5% simple interest per annum and partly at 10% simple interest per annum. Total interest received after 5 yr was ₹ 1750. Find the amount of money that was lent out at 10% simple interest per annum.
explain: Let $P$ be the sum lent at 10%. Then $(5000-P)$ is at 5%. $\frac{P \times 10 \times 5}{100} + \frac{(5000-P) \times 5 \times 5}{100} = 1750$. $\Rightarrow 0.5P + 1250 - 0.25P = 1750 \Rightarrow 0.25P = 500 \Rightarrow P = ₹ 2000$.

q: If the amount obtained by A, by investing ₹ 9100 for 3 yr at a rate of 10% p.a. on simple interest is equal to the amount obtained by B, by investing a certain sum of money for 5 yr at a rate of 8% p.a. on simple interest, then 90% of the sum invested by B (in ₹) is:
If ₹ 1000 be invested at interest rate of 5% and the interest be added to the principal every 10 yr, then the number of year in which it will amount to ₹ 2000 is:
explain: Interest for first 10 yr $= \frac{1000 \times 5 \times 10}{100} = ₹ 500$. New Principal after 10 yr $= 1500$. Remaining interest needed $= 2000 - 1500 = ₹ 500$. $500 = \frac{1500 \times 5 \times T}{100} \Rightarrow T = \frac{500}{75} = 6\frac{2}{3} \text{ yr}$. Total time $= 10 + 6\frac{2}{3} = 16\frac{2}{3} \text{ yr}$.

q: Mr Thomas invested an amount of ₹ 13900 divided in two different schemes A and B at the simple interest rate of 14% per annum and 11% per annum respectively. If the total amount of simple interest earned in 2 yr be ₹ 3508, what was the amount invested in scheme B?
explain: Let amount in B be $x$. Interest from B $= \frac{x \times 11 \times 2}{100}$. Interest from A $= \frac{(13900-x) \times 14 \times 2}{100}$. $0.22x + 3892 - 0.28x = 3508 \Rightarrow 0.06x = 384 \Rightarrow x = ₹ 6400$.

q: Mr Thomas invested an amount of ₹ 13900 divided in two different schemes A and B at the simple interest rate of 14% per annum and 11% per annum respectively. If the total amount of simple interest earned in 2 yr be ₹ 3508, what was the amount invested in scheme B?
explain: Let amount in B be $x$. Interest from B $= \frac{x \times 11 \times 2}{100}$. Interest from A $= \frac{(13900-x) \times 14 \times 2}{100}$. $0.22x + 3892 - 0.28x = 3508 \Rightarrow 0.06x = 384 \Rightarrow x = ₹ 6400$.

q: A sum of ₹ 5000 is divided into two parts such that the simple interest on the first part for 4 1/5 yr at 6 2/3% p.a. is double the simple interest on the second part for 2 3/4 yr at 4% p.a. The ratio of the second part to the first part is:

In a business dealing, A owes B ₹ 20000 payable after 5 yr, whereas B owes A ₹ 12000 payable after 4 yr. They want to settle it now at the rate of 5% simple interest. Who gives how much money in this settlement?
explain: Present Worth $(PW) = \frac{\text{Amount} \times 100}{100 + (R \times T)}$. $PW_A = \frac{20000 \times 100}{100 + (5 \times 5)} = ₹ 16000$. $PW_B = \frac{12000 \times 100}{100 + (5 \times 4)} = ₹ 10000$. A owes B more, so A pays $16000 - 10000 = ₹ 6000$ to B.

q: Rahim invested a certain sum at 5% simple interest for 3 yr. His friend Hiralal invested the same sum for 2 yr at 7% simple interest. Rahim got ₹ 30 more interest than Hiralal. What was the amount invested by them?
explain: Let sum be $P$. Interest difference $= \frac{P \times 5 \times 3}{100} - \frac{P \times 7 \times 2}{100} = 30$. $\Rightarrow 0.15P - 0.14P = 30 \Rightarrow 0.01P = 30 \Rightarrow P = ₹ 3000$.

q: The amount payable on maturity of a certain sum which is invested for 5 yr at a certain rate per cent p.a. is ₹ 9800 and the amount payable on the same sum invested for 10 yr at the same rate is ₹ 12600. The rate of interest p.a. is:

A milkman borrowed a sum of ₹ 2500 from two moneylenders for one loan on simple interest at the rate of 5% and 7%, respectively, for a period of 2 yr. If the total interest paid by him was ₹ 276, then how much did he borrow at the rate of 7% p.a.?

A sum of money of ₹ 2600 was lent out in two parts in such a way that the simple interest on the first part at 10% per annum for 5yr is the same as the interest of the second part at 9% per annum for 6 yr. The part lent out at 10% is:

The monthly income of Mr. Roy is ₹ 18000. He took a loan of ₹ 30000 on simple interest for 3 yr at the rate of 5% per annum. The amount that he will be paying as simple interest in 3 yr is what per cent of his monthly salary?

A certain sum invested at simple interest for 3 1/2 yr amounts to ₹ 6747 and for 5 yr amounts to ₹ 7410 at the same rate per cent per annum. The rate of interest per annum is:
explain: SI for $1.5 \text{ yr} = 7410 - 6747 = ₹ 663 \Rightarrow$ SI for $1 \text{ yr} = 442$. Principal $= 7410 - (5 \times 442) = ₹ 5200$. $R = \frac{442 \times 100}{5200} = 8.5\%$.

q: A sum of ₹ 10000 is taken as a loan by Rajesh at a rate of 15% p.a. simple interest for 2 yr. But Rajesh could not repay it and the lender included the interest amount as principal for the next two years. The total amount paid at the end of 4 yr is:
explain: SI (first 2 yr) $= \frac{10000 \times 15 \times 2}{100} = ₹ 3000$. New Principal for next 2 yr $= 13000$. SI (next 2 yr) $= \frac{13000 \times 15 \times 2}{100} = ₹ 3900$. Total Amount $= 13000 + 3900 = ₹ 16900$.

q: A sum of ₹ 50250 is divided into two parts such that, the simple interest on the first part for 7 1/2 yr at 8 1/3% per annum is 5/2 times the simple interest on the second part for 5 1/4 yr at 8% per annum. What is the difference (in ₹) between the two parts?
explain: $SI_1 = P_1 \times \frac{15}{2} \times \frac{25}{300} = \frac{5}{8}P_1$. $SI_2 = P_2 \times \frac{21}{4} \times \frac{8}{100} = \frac{42}{100}P_2$. Given $\frac{5}{8}P_1 = \frac{5}{2} \times \frac{42}{100}P_2 \Rightarrow P_1 = 1.68P_2$. $P_1 + P_2 = 50250 \Rightarrow 2.68P_2 = 50250 \Rightarrow P_2 = 18750, P_1 = 31500$. Difference $= ₹ 12750$.

q: Rajesh invested ₹ 10000 by dividing it into two different investment Schemes A and B, at simple interest rates of 8% and 10%, respectively. If the total interest earned in 2 yr is ₹ 1680, the amount invested in Scheme A is:

Two persons Amar and Baala lent out ₹ 15000 each at simple interest for 5 yr. The difference between the simple interest received by them is ₹ 3000. If the sum of the annual rates of interest is 11% per annum and Amar received more interest than Baala, then what is the interest received by Amar?
explain: Diff in rates $(R_1 - R_2) = \frac{3000 \times 100}{15000 \times 5} = 4\%$. Given $R_1 + R_2 = 11\%$. Solving: $R_1 = 7.5\%, R_2 = 3.5\%$. Interest for Amar $= 15000 \times 0.075 \times 5 = ₹ 5625$.

q: A trader owes a merchant ₹ 10500 due in one year. The trader wants to settle the account after four months. If the rate of interest is 6% per annum, then how much should he pay (rounded off value)?
explain: Settlement is 8 months before due date. $PW = \frac{10500 \times 100}{100 + (6 \times 8/12)} = \frac{1050000}{104} \approx ₹ 10096$.

q: A sum invested at the rate of 6% simple interest per annum grows to ₹ 113880 in 5 yr. What is the simple interest, if the same sum is invested for 8 yr at the rate of 9% per annum?
The simple interest on a certain sum for 4 yr at the rate of 15% p.a. is ₹ 4500 less than the simple interest on the same sum for 6 yr at the same rate of interest. Find the sum.

1/2 of a certain sum is lent at 20% rate of interest. 2/5 of the remaining sum is lent at 25% rate of interest. The remaining sum is lent at 10% rate of interest. If the total interest for 2 yr is ₹ 360, then what is the sum?
explain: Let sum be $P$. Parts: $0.5P$ at 20%, $0.2P$ (2/5 of 0.5) at 25%, and $0.3P$ at 10%. Interest $= 2[ (0.5 \times 0.2) + (0.2 \times 0.25) + (0.3 \times 0.1) ]P = 360$. $\Rightarrow 2[0.1 + 0.05 + 0.03]P = 360 \Rightarrow 0.36P = 360 \Rightarrow P = ₹ 1000$.

q: Find the compound interest on ₹11,000 in 2 yr at 4% p.a., interest compounded yearly.[RRB ALP 2024]
What is the compound interest on ₹25,000 for 3 yr at 10% p.a. compounded yearly?[SSC (10+2) 2023]
explain: Effective rate for 10% for 3 years is 33.1%. CI = 25000 * 33.1 / 100 = 8275.

q: What is the present worth of ₹9,261 due 3 yr from now at 5% p.a. compounded annually?[UP Police Head Operator 2024]

q: Three amounts x, y, z are such that y is the compound interest on x and z is the compound interest on y. The rate of interest per annum and the time period (in years) are same. Which of the following is correct?[CDS 2024]
explain: CI is proportional to Principal. y/x = rate part, z/y = rate part. Thus y/x = z/y => y^2 = zx.

An athlete runs 800 m in 96 sec. His speed is
explain: We know that, Speed = Distance / Time. Given, Distance = 800 m and Time = 96 sec. Speed of athlete = 800 / 96 m/sec = (800 / 96) * (18 / 5) km/h = 30 km/h.

q: A car takes 5 h to cover a distance of a certain journey at a speed of 30 km/h. What will be the speed of the car to cover the same distance in 2.5 h?
explain: Given, a car takes 5 h to cover a distance if the speed is 30 km/h. Total distance covered by car = 30 * 5 = 150 km. Speed to cover the same distance in 2.5 h = 150 km / 2.5 h = 60 km/h. Hence, the speed of car is 60 km/h.

q: The ratio between the time taken by three cars to cover the same distance is 12 : 15 : 10. The ratio between their speeds is
explain: Here, distance = constant. Then, Time ∝ 1 / Speed. Ratio of time = 12 : 15 : 10. Then, ratio of speed = 1/12 : 1/15 : 1/10. [LCM of 12, 15, 10 is 120] = 120 * (1/12) : 120 * (1/15) : 120 * (1/10) = 10 : 8 : 12 = 5 : 4 : 6. Hence, required ratio of speed is 5:4:6.

q: A man covers a certain distance on scooter. Had he moved 4 km/h faster, he would have taken 30 min less. If he moves 3 km/h slower, he would have taken 30 min more. Find the distance.
explain: Let the distance be d km. According to the question, d/40 + d/5 = 4.5 h => 9d/40 = 9/2 => d = 20 km. So, total distance = 20 * 2 = 40 km.

q: A man travels a distance of 240 km partly by train and partly by car. If he travels 60 km by train and the rest by car, then he takes 4 h to cover the distance. If he travels 80 km by train and the rest by car, then he takes 4 h 10 min. Find the speed of the train.
explain: Let the total distance be d km. According to the question, (d/4)/25 + (3d/4)/30 = 14 => d/100 + 3d/120 = 14 => d/100 + d/40 = 14 => (2d + 5d)/200 = 14 => 7d/200 = 14 => d = 2 * 200 = 400 km.

q: A boy travels a certain distance. He covers 25% of the distance at 3 km/h and the rest at 6 km/h. If total time taken is 10 h, then find the total distance.
explain: Let total distance be 4x km. According to the question, x/3 + 3x/6 = 10 h [since Time = Distance / Speed] => (2x + 3x)/6 = 10 => 5x/6 = 10 => x = (10 * 6) / 5 => x = 12. Hence, required distance = 4x = 4 * 12 = 48 km.

q: The speed of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 5. A takes 30 min more than B to reach the destination. In what time does A reach the destination?
explain: Given, speed ratio of A and B = 3:5. Time is inversely proportional to the speed. Therefore, Time taken by A:B = 5:3 [since Distance is constant]. Let time taken by A and B be 5x and 3x, respectively. Then, 5x - 3x = 30 min => 2x = 30 => x = 15 min. Time taken by A to reach destination = 5x = 5 * 15 min = 75 min = 1 h 15 min.

q: A car covers a distance of 40 km in 24 min. If its speed is decreased by 40 km/h, then what will be the time taken by the car to cover the same distance?
explain: Speed of car = Distance covered by car / Time taken = 40 km / (24/60) h = (40 * 60) / 24 km/h = 100 km/h. New speed = (100 - 40) km/h = 60 km/h. Now, time taken to cover 40 km = Distance / Speed = 40 / 60 h = (40 / 60) * 60 = 40 min.

q: Yug drives a car at speed of 56 km/h and covers a certain distance in 1.5 h. At what speed should he drive the car to cover the same distance in 7 h?
explain: Speed of Yug = 56 km/h and time = 3/2 h. Distance covered by Yug = 56 * (3/2) = 28 * 3 = 84 km. Now, required speed = 84 / 7 = 12 km/h.

q: A man covers half of his journey at 90 km/h and the remaining half at 30 km/h. If he takes 8 h in all, then find the total distance of the journey.
explain: Let the length of journey be d km. According to the question, (d/2)/90 + (d/2)/30 = 8 => d/180 + d/60 = 8 => (d + 3d)/180 = 8 => d = (8 * 180) / 4 = 360. Hence, required distance = 360 km.

q: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 60 km/h and including stoppages, it is 54 km/h. For how many minutes does the bus stop per hour?
explain: Excluding stoppage, the speed of the bus = 60 km/h. Distance covered in 1 h = 60 km. Similarly, including stoppage, distance covered in 1 h = 54 km. Now, the bus stops per hour for = [(60 - 54) / 60] * 60 min = 6 min.

q: A person travels 110 miles in 2 h, next 120 miles in 2 h and last 60 miles in 1 h. Find his average speed.
explain: According to the question, For 110 miles he takes 2 h, For next 120 miles he takes 2 h, For last 60 miles he takes 1 h. So, average speed = Total distance covered / Total time taken = (110 + 120 + 60) / (2 + 2 + 1) = 290 / 5 = 58 miles/h.

q: A person has to cover a distance of 150 km in 12 h. If he covers 2/3 of the distance in 5/8 of the total time, then find the speed to cover the remaining distance in the remaining time.
explain: Total distance to cover is 150 km. Total time 12 h. Distance covered = 150 * (2/3) = 100 km. So, remaining distance = 150 - 100 = 50 km. Time consumed in covering 100 km = 12 * (5/8) = 3 * (5/2) = 15/2 = 7.5 h. Remaining time = 12 - 7.5 = 4.5 h. Required speed to cover remaining distance = 50 / 4.5 = 500 / 45 = 100 / 9 = 11.11 km/h. Hence, required speed = 11.11 km/h.

q: Four cars are moving with speeds 2u, 3u, 4u and xu. The time taken by these cars to cover the same distance is xt, 4t, 3t and 2t, respectively. Find the value of x.
explain: Speed of cars are 2u, 3u, 4u and xu. Time taken by cars are xt, 4t, 3t and 2t. Here, distance is same for all cars. Thus, 2u * xt = 3u * 4t = 4u * 3t = xu * 2t [since Distance = Speed * Time]. Taking 2u * xt = 3u * 4t => 2 * x = 12 => Thus, value of x is 6.

q: An aeroplane covers a distance from 12000 km to 12800 km in 4 h. Find its average speed in m/sec.
explain: Total distance covered = 12800 - 12000 = 800 km. Total time = 4 h. Therefore, Average speed = Total distance covered / Total time taken = 800 / 4 = 200 km/h = 200 * (5/18) = 500 / 9 m/sec.

q: A car covers a certain distance at 30 km/h and returns at 45 km/h. Find its average speed.
explain: If distance is same, the average speed = 2xy / (x + y). Here, x = 30 km/h, y = 45 km/h. Average speed = (2 * 30 * 45) / (30 + 45) = 36 km/h.

q: A bus travels for 3 h at 60 km/h, 4 h at 50 km/h and 5 h at 50 km/h. Find its average speed.
explain: Given, Distance covered by bus at 60 km/h = 60 * 3 = 180 km. Distance covered by bus at 50 km/h = 50 * 4 = 200 km. Distance covered by bus at 50 km/h = 50 * 5 = 250 km. Therefore, Average speed = Total distance / Total time = (180 + 200 + 250) / (3 + 4 + 5) = 630 / 12 = 52.5 km/h.

q: A man covers half of his journey at 45 km/h and the rest at 36 km/h. Find his average speed.
explain: Here, A = 45 km/h and B = 36 km/h. Therefore, Average speed = 2AB / (A + B) = (2 * 45 * 36) / 81 = (2 * 5 * 36) / 9 = 40 km/h.

q: A person covers a distance of 100 km. He covers first 50 km at 50 km/h, next 25 km at 50 km/h and last 25 km at 25 km/h. Find his average speed.
A truck covers three distances of 220 km, 250 km and 140 km at speeds of 11 km/h, 5 km/h and 7 km/h, respectively. Find its average speed.
explain: Total distance = 220 + 250 + 140 = 610 km. Total time taken = 220/11 + 250/5 + 140/7 = 20 + 50 + 20 = 90 h. Average speed = 610 / 90 = 6_7/9 km/h.

q: A body covers distances of 3 km, 7 km and 32 km at speeds of 2 km/h, 4 km/h and 28 km/h, respectively. Find its average speed.
explain: Total time = 3/2 + 7/4 + 32/28 = (42 + 49 + 32) / 28 = 123/28 h. Total distance = 3 + 7 + 32 = 42 km. Average speed = Total distance / Total time = 42 / (123/28) = (42 / 123) * 28 = 392 / 41 km/h.

q: A vehicle covers a distance of 60 km at 40 km/h and next 90 km at 45 km/h. Find its average speed.
explain: We know that, Average speed = Total distance / Total time, where Time = Distance / Speed. Average speed = (60 + 90) / (60/40 + 90/45) = 150 / (3/2 + 2/1) = 150 / ((3 + 4)/2) = 300 / 7 = 42_6/7 km/h.

q: An object moves 20 m in 5 min and next 30 km at a speed of 50 km/h. Find its average speed.
explain: Object moves 20 m in 5 min and 30 km with speed of 50 km/h. So, total distance = 20 + 30 * 1000 = 20 + 30000 = 30020 m. Total time = 5 * 60 + (30/50) * 60 * 60 = 300 + 0.6 * 3600 = 300 + 2160 = 2460 sec. Average speed = 30020 / 2460 = 12.2 m/sec.

q: A person covers 75 km at 45 km/h and next 45 km at 70 km/h. Find his average speed.
A car covers four successive 3 km stretches at speeds of 10 km/h, 20 km/h, 30 km/h and 60 km/h, respectively. Find its average speed.
explain: As we know, Average speed = Total distance / Total time = (3 + 3 + 3) / (3/10 + 3/20 + 3/30 + 3/60) = 9 / ((18 + 9 + 6 + 3)/60) = (9 * 60) / 36 = 15 km/h. (Note: Alternative textbook calculation using full journey stretches evaluates contextually to 20 km/h).

q: A tourist travels from Dehradun to Mussoorie (35 km) at 36 km/h and returns at 60 km/h. Find his average speed for the entire journey.
explain: Total distance between Dehradun to Mussoorie is 35 km. Time taken from Dehradun to Mussoorie = 35/36 h. Time taken from Mussoorie to Dehradun (returning) = 35/60 = 7/12 h. Average speed = (2 * 35) / (35/36 + 7/12) = 70 / (56/36) = (70 * 36) / 56 = 45 km/h. Fast Track Method: Here, x = 36 km/h and y = 60 km/h. Then, average speed = 2xy / (x + y) = (2 * 36 * 60) / (36 + 60) = 45 km/h.

q: A man travels a certain distance. He covers 1/3 part at 10 km/h, 1/4 part at 15 km/h and the remaining part at 20 km/h. Find his average speed.
explain: Let the total distance be x km. Time taken to cover 1/3 part = (x/3)/10 = x/30 h. Time taken to cover 1/4 part = (x/4)/15 = x/60 h. Time taken to cover rest part = (x - (x/3 + x/4)) / 20 = 5x / (12 * 20) = x/48 h. Therefore, Average speed = Total distance / Total time = x / (x/30 + x/60 + x/48) = 240 / (8 + 4 + 5) = 240 / 17 km/h. Fast Track Method: P = 1/3, Q = 1/4, R = 5/12, X = 10, Y = 15, Z = 20. Average speed = 1 / ((1/3)/10 + (1/4)/15 + (5/12)/20) = 1 / (1/30 + 1/60 + 5/240) = 1 / (17/240) = 240/17 km/h.

q: A person covers a certain distance in three equal parts at speeds of 40 km/h, 50 km/h and 60 km/h, respectively. Find his average speed.
A person travels 550 km by train at 55 km/h, 4500 km by plane at 500 km/h, 400 km by boat at 25 km/h and 55 km by auto at 35 km/h. Find his average speed for the entire journey.
explain: Time taken by train = 550/55 = 10 h. Time taken by plane = 4500/500 = 9 h. Time taken by boat = 400/25 = 16 h. Time taken by auto = 55/35 = 11/7 h. Total distance = 550 + 4500 + 400 + 55 = 5505 km. Total time = 10 + 9 + 16 + 11/7 = 256/7 h. Average speed = Total distance / Total time = 5505 / (256/7) = (5505 * 7) / 256 = 150_136/256 km/h.

q: The average speed of a person from city A to B is 280/11 km/h. He travels at 20 km/h for the first half time and at q km/h for the second half time. Also, his average speed from city B to C is 112/3 km/h, where he travels at q km/h for the first half distance and at r km/h for the second half distance. Find the values of q and r.
A man walks a certain distance at 5 km/h in 3 h 45 min. If he runs the same distance on a cycle at a certain speed in 2 h 10 min, then find the speed of the cycle.
explain: Speed of man = 5 km/h. Time taken = 3 h 45 min = 3_3/4 h. Distance covered = Speed * Time = 5 * (15/4) = 75/4 km. Now, time taken by cycle = 2 h 10 min = 2_1/6 = 13/6 h. Speed of the cycle = Total distance / Time taken by cycle = (75/4) / (13/6) = 450 / 52 = 8_17/26 km/h.

q: Shilpa drives a car for 3 h at 20 km/h. She decides to return immediately and drives back at 15 km/h. Find her average speed for the entire journey.
explain: Distance travelled by Shilpa in 3 h = 20 * 3 = 60 km. According to the question, time required to cover 60 km with speed of 15 km/h = 60 / 15 = 4 h. Total time = 3 + 4 = 7 h. Total distance = 60 * 2 = 120 km. Hence, average speed of Shilpa = 120 / 7 = 17_1/7 km/h. Fast Track Method: Average speed = (2 * 20 * 15) / (20 + 15) = 2 * (300 / 35) = 17_1/7 km/h.

q: A person goes to his office from his home at a certain speed and returns back at a speed 3 times his original speed. If his average speed for the entire journey is 18 km/h, find his speed while going to office.
explain: Let distance between home and office be d km and speed of returning be 3x km/h. Then speed of going to office is 3x * (1/3) = x km/h. Average speed = Total distance / Total time => 18 = (d + d) / (d/x + d/3x) => 18 = 2d / (4d/3x) => 18 = (2d/4d) * 3x => 18 = 3x/2 => x = 12 km/h. Hence, required speed to go to office is 12 km/h. Fast Track Method: Going speed = x, returning speed = 3x. Average speed = (2 * x * 3x) / (x + 3x) => 6x^2 / 4x = 18 => x = 12 km/h.

q: A person covers a distance in four equal parts. He covers first part at 30 km/h, second part at 36 km/h and last two parts at y km/h. If his average speed for the entire journey is 37_7/29 km/h, find the value of y.
explain: Let total distance be 4d. According to the question, Average speed = Total distance / Total time => 37_7/29 = 4d / (d/30 d/36 + 2d/y) => 1080/29 = 4 / (1/30 + 1/36 + 2/y) => 116 = 36 + 30 + 2160/y => 50 = 2160/y => y = 216 / 5 = 43.2 km/h.

q: A train covers a distance of 300 km at 75 km/h, next 90 km at 45 km/h and remaining 390 km at x km/h. If its average speed for the entire journey is 43_1/3 km/h, find the value of x.
A car travels for 45 min at 80 km/h, next 40 min at 48 km/h and remaining 35 min at x km/h. If its average speed for the entire journey is 72_1/4 km/h, find the value of x.
A person covers 25% of his journey at 25 km/h, 50% at 50 km/h and the remaining part at 12.5 km/h. Find his average speed for the entire journey.
explain: Let total distance be 100 km. According to the question, remaining 25% of total distance covered by 12.5 km/h. Now, time taken for 25% of total distance = 25/25 = 1 h. Time taken for 50% of total distance = 50/50 = 1 h. Time taken for remaining 25% of total distance = 25/12.5 = 2 h. Then, average speed = Total distance / Total time = 100 / (1 + 1 + 2) = 100 / 4 = 25 km/h.

q: A person covers 40% of his journey at 8 km/h, 40% of the remaining journey at 9 km/h and the rest at 12 km/h. Find his average speed.
explain: Let total distance be 100x km. 40% of total distance = 40x km. 40% of remaining distance = (100x - 40x) * (40/100) = 24x km. Remaining distance = 100x - 40x - 24x = 36x km. Required time to cover 40% distance with speed of 8 km/h = 40x / 8 = 5x h. Required time to cover 40% of remaining distance with speed of 9 km/h = 24x / 9 = 8x/3 h. Required time to cover rest distance with speed of 12 km/h = 36x / 12 = 3x h. Therefore, Average speed = 100x / (5x + 8x/3 + 3x) = 100 / ((15 + 8 + 9)/3) = 300 / 32 = 9_3/8 km/h.

q: Two cars A and B travel from Chennai to Bangalore. Car B starts at a speed of 80 km/h and takes 20 h. Car A takes 25 h to cover the same distance. Find the speed of Car A.
explain: Speed of B = 80 km/h, Time taken by B = 20 h. Let speed of A be x km/h, Time taken by A = 25 h. Distance between Chennai and Bangalore = 80 * 20 = 1600 km. Speed of Car A = 1600 / 25 = 64 km/h.

q: A man walks at a certain speed for 30 h. If he decreases his speed by 1/15th, he covers 10 km less in the same time. Find his original speed.
explain: Let his speed be 15x km/h and time = 30 h. Then, according to the question, 15x * 30 - 14x * 30 = 10 => 450x - 420x = 10 => 30x = 10 => x = 1/3. Then, required speed = 15x = 15 * (1/3) = 5 km/h.

q: A person drives from his home to office at 40 km/h and returns at 45 km/h. If he takes 1 h more while going to office than returning, find the distance between his home and office.
explain: Let the distance drove in each way be x km. x/40 - x/45 = 1 => (9x - 8x) / 360 = 1 => x = 360 km. Option (e) is correct because the answer is 360 km.

q: A boy walks from his home to school at 3 km/h and reaches 20 min late. Next day he walks at 4 km/h and reaches 30 min early. Find the distance between his home and school.
A car covers a distance of 60 km at a uniform speed. If the speed is increased by 8 km/h, it takes 2 h less to cover the distance. Find the original speed of the car.
explain: Let the original speed of car be x km/h. Time taken to travel 60 km = 60/x h. If speed is increased by 8 km/h, then time taken to travel 60 km = 60/(x+8) h. According to the question, 60/x - 60/(x+8) = 2 => 60(x + 8) - 60x = 2x(x + 8) => 480 = 2x^2 + 16x => x^2 + 8x - 240 = 0 => (x + 20)(x - 12) = 0 => x = 12 km/h.

q: A student walks from his starting point to college at 5 km/h and reaches 12 min late. Next day he walks at 8 km/h and reaches 15 min early. Find the distance.
explain: Let the distance between his college and his starting point be x km. According to the question, x/5 - 12/60 = x/8 + 15/60 => x/5 - x/8 = 15/60 + 12/60 => 3x/40 = 27/60 => 3x = (27/60) * 40 => x = (27 * 40) / (60 * 3) = 6 km. Fast Track Method: Here, a = 5 km/h, t1 = 12 min, b = 8 km/h, t2 = 15 min. Required distance = [ab / (b - a)] * [(t1 + t2)/60] = [5 * 8 / (8 - 5)] * [(12 + 15)/60] = (40/3) * (27/60) = 6 km.

q: A person covers a distance between city X and Y. If he drives at 12 km/h, he reaches 60 min late. If he drives at 18 km/h, he reaches 60 min early. Find the distance between city X and Y.
explain: Let the distance between X and Y be d km. According to the question, d/12 - d/18 = 2 h (since 60 min early + 60 min late = 120 min = 2 h) => d * [(3 - 2)/36] = 2 => d * (1/36) = 2 => d = 72 km.

q: A boy walks from his hostel to college. If he walks at 15 km/h, he reaches 2 min late. If he walks at 20 km/h, he reaches 2 min early. Find the distance between hostel and college.
explain: Let total time of journey be t h, distance is constant. s1 * t1 = s2 * t2 => 15 * (t + 2/60) = 20 * (t - 2/60) = > 3t + 1/10 = 4t - 4/30 => 7/30 = t. Total time of journey is 7/30 h. Then, distance between hostel and college = 15 * (7/30 + 2/60) = 15 * (16/60) = 4 km. Fast Track Method: Speed ratio 15:20 => 3:4. Time ratio 4:3. Difference = 1 unit -> 4 min (2 + 2). 4 units -> 16 min. Required distance = 15 * (16/60) = 4 km.

q: A car covers a distance in three equal parts at speeds of 40 km/h, 45 km/h and 60 km/h, respectively. Find its average speed.
explain: Let distance = d. According to the question, t1 = d/40, t2 = d/45, t3 = d/60. Average speed = Total distance / Total time = (d + d + d) / (d/40 + d/45 + d/60) = 3d / ((90d + 80d + 60d)/3600) = (3d * 3600) / 230d = 1080 / 23 = 46.96 km/h.

q: A thief steals a car at 3 pm and drives it at 50 km/h. The theft is discovered at 4 pm and the owner chases him in another car at 70 km/h. At what time will the owner catch the thief?
explain: Speed of thief = 50 km/h. Distance covered by thief in 1 h = 50 km. Speed of owner = 70 km/h. Relative speed of thief and owner = (70 - 50) = 20 km/h. Owner will catch the thief after = 50 / 20 = 5/2 h = 2 h 30 min. Hence, required time when owner catches thief = 4 pm + 2 h 30 min = 6:30 pm.

q: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 200 m. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is 7 km/h and that of the policeman is 8 km/h, find the distance covered by the policeman to catch the thief.
explain: Speed of thief is 7 km/h and speed of policeman is 8 km/h. Thief ran only for 6 min, so distance covered in 6 min by thief = 7 * (5/18) * 6 * 60 = 700 m. Relative speed = 8 - 7 = 1 km/h = 5/18 m/sec. Time required to catch the thief = 700 / (5/18) = (700 * 18) / 5 sec = (140 * 18) / 60 = 42 min. Now, distance covered by policeman in 42 min with 8 km/h = 8 * (42/60) = 5.6 km.

q: A thief is at point X. A policeman starts chasing him from point X at 30 km/h after 30 min. The thief sees the policeman when he is 10 km away from X and runs back towards X at 25 km/h. If the initial separation between them at that moment is 400 m, find the distance from point X where the thief is caught.
explain: Thief ran with speed of 20 km/h initially. Distance travelled in 30 min = 20 * (1/2) = 10 km. After 10 km, thief saw policeman and returned with speed of 25 km/h. Initial separation distance between thief and policeman is 400 m = 0.4 km. Now, time required to catch the thief = 0.4 / (30 - 25) = 0.4 / 5 = 0.08 h. Distance travelled by thief before being caught = 25 * 0.08 = 2.00 km. Hence, required distance from point X is 10 - 2 = 8 km.

q: A police jeep is chasing a culprit who is running on a motorbike. The culprit is 12 m ahead of the police jeep. The speed of the police jeep is 18 m/s and it takes 18 sec to catch the culprit. If the total distance covered by the jeep is 864 m, find the speed of the motorbike.
Walking at 7/8th of his usual speed, Ansh covers a distance of 35 km in 50 min. Find his usual speed.
explain: Let usual speed be 8s km/h. Then, 7/8 of usual speed = 7s km/h. According to the question, 35 / 7s = 50 / 60 => 5 / s = 5 / 6 => s = 6. Hence, Ansh's usual speed is 8s = 8 * 6 = 48 km/h.

q: A vehicle covers a distance of 1800 km. If its speed is decreased by 10 km/h, it takes 2 h more to cover the distance. Find the original time taken by the vehicle.
explain: Let the speed of vehicle be x km/h. Total distance = 1800 km. According to the question, 1800/(x - 10) - 1800/x = 2 => 1800 * [(x - (x - 10)) / (x(x - 10))] = 2 => 18000 / (x^2 - 10x) = 2 => 9000 = x^2 - 10x => x^2 - 10x - 9000 = 0 => (x - 100)(x + 90) = 0 => x = 100 km/h. Now, required time = 1800 / 100 = 18 h.

q: A robber robs a bank at 5:00 pm and runs at 10 km/h. The police start chasing him from the bank at 5:12 pm at 15 km/h. At what time will the police catch the robber?
explain: Distance travelled by robber in 12 min = Speed * Time = 10 * (12/60) = 2 km. Time taken to chase the robber = Distance between both / Relative speed = 2 / (15 - 10) = 2/5 h = (2/5) * 60 min = 24 min. Hence, required time = 5:12 pm + 24 min = 5:36 pm.

q: A man walks at 60% of his original speed and reaches his destination 1 h 40 min late. Find his usual time to reach the destination.
explain: Let speed of man = 5x. 60% of speed = 5x * (3/5) = 3x. Ratio of speed before and after = 5x : 3x. Since speed is inversely proportional to time, time ratio before and after = 3x : 5x. According to the question, 5x - 3x = 1 h 40 min = 1_40/60 h => 2x = 5/3 => x = 5/6 h. Therefore, Required time = 3x = 3 * (5/6) = 5/2 = 2_1/2 h.

q: A person goes to his office at 30 km/h and reaches 10 min late. If he goes at 24 km/h, he reaches 18 min late. Find the distance between his home and office.
explain: Let correct time to reach office be x h. According to the question, 30 * (x + 10/60) = 24 * (x + 18/60) => 30x + 5 = 24x + 36/5 => 6x = 36/5 - 5 => 6x = 11/5 => x = 11/30 h. Therefore, Required distance = 30 * (11/30 + 10/60) = 30 * (32/60) = 16 km. Fast Track Method: a = 30, b = 24, t1 = 10 min late, t2 = 18 min late. Distance = [a * b / (a - b)] * [(t2 - t1)/60] = [30 * 24 / (30 - 24)] * [(18 - 10)/60] = (720 / 6) * (8 / 60) = 16 km.

q: A person increases his speed to 11/6th of his original speed and reaches his office 20 min early. Find his usual time.
explain: Let usual time be t, distance be d and original speed be s. Then, d = s * t = st ---(i) and d = (11/6)s * (t - 20) ---(ii). From Eqs. (i) and (ii), st = (11/6)s * (t - 20) => 6t = 11t - 220 => 5t = 220 => t = 44 min. Fast Track Method: x/y = 11/6, t = 20 min. Required time = (t * x) / (x - y) = (20 * 11) / (11 - 6) = 220 / 5 = 44 min.

q: A car covers a certain distance at a certain speed. If it moves at 3/4th of its original speed, it takes 1 h more. Find its usual time.
explain: Let original speed of car be 4x. Speed driven = (3/4) * 4x = 3x. Let usual time be t h. According to the question, 4x * t = 3x * (t + 1) => 4t = 3t + 3 => t = 3 h. Fast Track Method: x = 3, y = 4, t = 1 h. Usual Time = (t * x) / (y - x) = (1 * 3) / (4 - 3) = 3 h.

q: Ram and Shyam start at the same time from two points towards each other. After crossing each other, Ram takes 2 h and Shyam takes 8 h to reach their destinations. If Ram's speed is 40 km/h, find Shyam's speed.
explain: Speed of Ram is 40 km/h. By formula, Speed of Ram / Speed of Shyam = sqrt(Time of Shyam / Time of Ram) => 40 / Speed of Shyam = sqrt(8 / 2) = sqrt(4 / 1) = 2 / 1 => Speed of Shyam = 20 km/h.

q: Two cities A and B are 240 km apart. Two cars start from A and B towards each other. The ratio of their speeds is 5 : 7. If the speed of car B is 84 km/h, after how many minutes will they meet?
explain: Given, total distance = 240 km, ratio of speed A and B = 5:7. Let speeds be 5x and 7x. Given Speed of B = 84 km/h => 7x = 84 => x = 12. Speed of A = 5x = 5(12) = 60 km/h. Therefore, A and B will meet after = 240 / (84 + 60) = 240 / 144 = 20 / 12 = 5/3 h = (5/3) * 60 = 100 min.

q: Two cars are 20 km apart. If they travel in the same direction, they meet in 1 h. If they travel in opposite directions, they meet in 12 min. Find their speeds.
explain: Let the speed of first car be x km/h and second car be y km/h. Case I (Same direction): relative speed = (x - y) km/h, Distance = 20 km, Time = 1 h => x - y = 20/1 => x - y = 20 ---(i). Case II (Opposite direction): relative speed = (x + y) km/h, Distance = 20 km, Time = 12 min = 1/5 h => x + y = 20 / (1/5) => x + y = 100 ---(ii). Adding (i) and (ii): 2x = 120 => x = 60. From (i), y = 60 - 20 = 40. Speed of cars = 60, 40 (in km/h).

q: A car covers a distance of 280 km. If its speed is decreased by 14 km/h, it takes 1 h more to cover the same distance. Find its usual speed.
explain: Let usual speed of the car be x km/h. According to the question, x = 280/t and (x - 14) = 280/(t + 1) => x - 14 = 280 / (280/x + 1) => (x - 14) * ((280 + x)/x) = 280 => (x - 14)(280 + x) = 280x => 280x + x^2 - 3920 - 14x = 280x => x^2 - 14x - 3920 = 0 => (x - 70)(x + 56) = 0 => x = 70 km/h (speed cannot be negative).

q: Two men start from cities P and Q (181 km apart) towards each other. The first man starts from P at 8:30 am at 30 km/h. The second man starts from Q at 8:54 am at 35 km/h. At what time will they meet?
explain: Total distance between P and Q = 181 km. Total time from 8:30 am to 8:54 am = 24 min. Distance covered by 1st man upto 8:54 am = 30 * (24/60) = 12 km. Therefore, remaining distance between both men = 181 - 12 = 169 km. Meeting time of both men = Distance / Relative speed = 169 / (30 + 35) = 169 / 65 h = (169 / 65) * 60 = 156 min. Hence, they will meet at 8:54 am + 156 min = 11:30 am.

q: Parvez starts from city X to Y at 6:00 pm and reaches at 7:30 pm. He covers 1/4th of the distance at 4/5th of his usual speed. At what ratio of his usual speed should he cover the remaining distance to reach on time?
explain: Let total distance be d km. Time taken = 7:30 pm - 6 pm = 1.5 h = 3/2 h. Speed of Parvez = d / 1.5 = 2d/3 km/h. He travels 1/4 of distance with 4/5 of usual speed. Remaining distance = d - d/4 = 3d/4 km. Changed speed = (2d/3) * (4/5) = 8d/15 km/h. Time taken to travel (d/4) = (d/4) / (8d/15) = 15/32 h. Remaining time = 3/2 - 15/32 = 33/32 h. Required speed for remaining distance = (3d/4) / (33/32) = 8d/11 km/h. Required ratio of speed = (8d/11) / (2d/3) = 12/11.

q: In a 1200 m race, Rakesh beats Rajesh by 120 m. If Rakesh's speed is 40 m/s, find Rajesh's speed.
explain: Here, distance is constant, so speed ∝ 1/Time. Rakesh's speed is 40 m/sec, Rajesh's speed is 36 m/sec. Total Distance = 1200 m. Distance by which Rakesh beats Rajesh = (1200 / 40) * (40 - 36) = 30 * 4 = 120 m.

q: In a 100 m race, A beats B by 20 m and B beats C by 5 m. By how many meters does A beat C?
explain: Let A complete the race in 't' sec. Speed of A = 100/t m/s. Speed of B = (100 - 20)/t = 80/t m/s. Time taken by B to complete 100 m race = 100 / (80/t) = 5t/4. Speed of C = (100 - 5) / (5t/4) = (95 * 4)/5t = 76/t m/s. Now, A beats C by a distance = (100/t - 76/t) * t = 24 m. Fast Track Method: Distance ratios: A:B = 100:80, B:C = 100:95 => 20:19. Combined ratio: A:B:C = 25:20:19 => 100:80:76. Thus, when A covers 100m, C covers 76m, beating C by 100 - 76 = 24 meters.

q: Anil and Arun run around a circular track of length 2575 m. Their speeds are 72 km/h and 90 km/h, respectively. If they run in the same direction, after how many seconds will they meet for the first time?
explain: Given, length of track = 2575 m. Speed of Anil = 72 km/h = 72 * (5/18) = 20 m/sec. Speed of Arun = 90 km/h = 90 * (5/18) = 25 m/sec. Relative speed of Anil and Arun (same direction) = 25 - 20 = 5 m/sec. Time taken to meet first time = 2575 / 5 = 515 sec.

q: P can run a 400 m race in 120 sec. He beats Q by 20 m while Q takes 13 sec more than P to finish the race. Find Q's speed in km/h.
explain: Time taken by P to complete the race = Distance / Speed = 400 / (12 * 5/18) = 120 sec. According to the question, the speed of Q = (400 - 20) / (120 + 13) = 380 / 133 m/s = (380 / 133) * (18 / 5) = 10.29 km/h.

q: Two persons start running around a circular track of length 1.2 km from the same point in the same direction at speeds of 27 km/h and 18 km/h. After how many minutes will they meet?
explain: Given, distance = 1.2 km. Relative speed (same direction) = 27 - 18 = 9 km/h. Time = (1.2 / 9) * 60 = 8 min.

q: P and R start running around a circular track from the same point at the same time. P takes 12 min to complete one round and R takes 18 min. If they start at 12:30 pm in the same direction, at what time will they meet at the starting point for the 3rd time?
explain: Given, time taken by P to complete one round = 12 min. Time taken by R to complete one round = 18 min. LCM of 12 and 18 = 36 min. So, they meet each other after every 36 min. If they first meet at 12:30 pm, they will meet again at 12:30 + 36 + 36 + 36 = 2:18 pm.

q: Two cyclists start running around a circular track of length 2200 m from the same point at speeds of 20 km/h and 16 km/h in opposite directions. After how many seconds will they meet for the first time?
explain: Relative speed (opposite direction) = 20 + 16 = 36 km/h = 36 * (5/18) = 10 m/s. They will meet first time = 2200 / 10 = 220 sec = 3 min 40 sec.

q: A and B run around a circular track. Speed of A is 2 rounds/h and speed of B is 3 rounds/h. They start from the same point at 8:00 am in opposite directions. How many times will they cross each other by 9:30 am?
explain: Speed of A is 2 rounds/h, Speed of B is 3 rounds/h. Relative speed of A and B (opposite direction) = 3 + 2 = 5 rounds/h. From 8:00 am to 9:30 am = 1.5 h. Number of times they will cross each other till 9:30 am = (3/2) * 5 = 7.5 times ≈ 7 times. Hence, meeting number of times is 7.

q: Four runners complete one round of a circular track in 400 sec, 600 sec, 720 sec and 900 sec, respectively. After how many seconds will they meet at the starting point for the first time?
explain: Time taken by runners to complete one round of circular track are 400 sec, 600 sec, 720 sec and 900 sec, respectively. Therefore, time after which they meet at the starting point for the first time = LCM of (400, 600, 720 and 900) = 3600 sec.

q: P and Q run around a circular track of length 240 m at speeds of 15 m/min and 20 m/min, respectively. After how many minutes will they meet at the starting point?
explain: Total circular path is 240 m. Speed of P and Q is 15 m/min and 20 m/min. Then, time when they meet again at starting point = LCM of (240/15, 240/20) = LCM(16, 12) = 48 min.

q: Two cars run around a circular track of length 120 m at speeds of 20 m/s and 12 m/s in the same direction. How many times will they meet anywhere on the track before they meet at the starting point for the first time?
explain: Time to meet at starting point = LCM of (120/20, 120/12) = LCM of (6, 10) = 30 min. They will meet at starting point after every 30 min. Time to meet anywhere on track = 120 / (20 - 12) = 120 / 8 = 15 min. Number of times they meet in one loop sequence = 30 / 15 = 2 times.

q: X and Y run around a circular track of circumference 3600 m at speeds of 150 m/min and 180 m/min, respectively. If they run in the same direction, after how many minutes will they meet at the starting point?
explain: Circumference of track is 3600 m. Speed of X and Y are 150 m/min and 180 m/min, respectively. Time taken by X = 3600/150 = 24 min. Time taken by Y = 3600/180 = 20 min. Therefore, time taken by X and Y to meet at starting point = LCM of (24, 20) = 120 min.

q: 5 pipes are required to fill a tank in 1 h and 40 min. How long (in minutes) will it take to fill the same tank if 4 pipes of the same type are used? [SSC MTS 2023]
explain: 1 h and 40 min = 100 min. Let the efficiency of one pipe be $p$. Total work = $5p \times 100$. For 4 pipes: $5p \times 100 = 4p \times x \Rightarrow x = \frac{500}{4} = 125$ min.

q: 27 bucket of water are required to fill a tank completely. If the capacity of the bucket is reduced to three-fourth of its current capacity, then how many bucket of water will be required to fill this tank completely. [DSSSB 2019]
explain: Let capacity of bucket be $t$. Tank capacity = $27t$. New bucket capacity = $\frac{3}{4}t$. Required buckets = $27t / (\frac{3}{4}t) = 27 \times \frac{4}{3} = 36$.

q: 6 pipes, all of the same type, are required to fill a tank in 1 h 20 min. How long will it take if only 5 pipes of the same type are used? [RRB NTPC 2021]
explain: 1 h 20 min = 80 min. Total work = $6 \times 80 = 480$ unit-min. Time for 5 pipes = $\frac{480}{5} = 96$ min = 1 h 36 min.

q: Two inlet pipes A and B can fill the tank in 3 h. C is the outlet pipe. Together A, B and C and fill the tank in 4 h. Find in how many hours, pipe C can empty the tank. [IBPS Clerk (Pre) 2022]
explain: Part filled by A+B in 1h = $\frac{1}{3}$. Part filled by A+B+C in 1h = $\frac{1}{4}$. Part emptied by C in 1h = $\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{12}$. Time for C = 12 h.

q: A tank is filled by three pipes A, B and C in 4 h. Pipe C is twice as fast as pipe B, and pipe B is twice as fast as pipe A. How much time will be taken by pipe A to fill the tank? [RRB Group D 2022]
explain: Efficiency ratio A:B:C = $1:2:4$. Total efficiency = 7. Capacity = $7 \times 4 = 28$ units. Time for A = $\frac{28}{1} = 28$ h.

q: An inlet pipe can fill the tank in 4 h and an outlet pipe can empty the tank in 6 h. By mistake, both the pipes are kept open. Find the number of hours in which the tank will be half-filled. [RRB NTPC 2021]
explain: Net fill in 1h = $\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{12}$. Full tank takes 12h. Half tank takes $\frac{12}{2} = 6$ h.

q: P can fill a tank in 5 h. Q can fill the same tank in 10 h. R can empty the same tank in 20 h. How much time (in house) will all the three take together to fill the same tank? [SSC (10+2) 2023]

An inlet pipe can fill an empty tank in 3.6 h, while an outlet pipe can drain a completely-filled tank in 6.3 h. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously when the tank is empty, in how many hours will the tank get completely filled? [SSC CPO 2023]
Two pipes X and Y can fill a tank in 12 min and 18 min, respectively. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, how long will it take to fill the tank (in minutes)? [SSC Selection Post 2022]
Two pipes can fill a tank in 2 h and 3 h, separately. If both pipes are opened together, then the tank will be filled in [CGPSC 2019]

An inlet pipe can fill an empty tank in 51 h while an outlet pipe drains a completely-filled tank in 76.5 h. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously when the tank is empty, in how many hours will the tank get completely filled? [SSC (10+2) 2023]

Tap P can fill a cistern in 6 h and tap Q can empty the full cistern in 10 h. If both taps P and Q are kept open simultaneously, then in how many hours will the empty cistern be completely fully? [SSC (10+2) 2021]
A cistern can be filled in 9 h. But due to a leak, it takes one hour more. If the cistern is full, in what time will it become empty due to the leak? [RRB JE 2019]
explain: Fill rate = $\frac{1}{9}$, Net rate (with leak) = $\frac{1}{10}$. Leak rate = $\frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{10} = \frac{1}{90}$. Time = 90 h.

q: Pipe L can fill a pool in 30 h and pipe M in 45 h. If both the pipes are opened in an empty pool, how much time will they take to fill it? [SSC CGL (Tier-1) 2024]

A cistern has three pipes A, B and C. A and B alone can completely fill the cistern in 4 h and 3 h, respectively and C can empty the completely filled cistern in 2 h. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously in the empty cistern, then the cistern will get completely full in: [RRB Group D 2022]

Pipe A can empty a tank in 64 min, Pipe B can fill the same tank in 96 min and Pipe C can fill the same tank in 128 min. If all three pipes are opened together. How many minutes will it take to fill the empty tank? [UP Police SI 2021]

Two pipes A and B can fill the tank in 5 h and 8 h respectively. Pipe C can empty the same tank in 10 h. Find the time taken to fill the empty tank when all the pipes are opened simultaneously. [RRB Group D 2022]

If pipe A can fill a cistern in X h, pipe B can fill the same cistern in Y h, and pipe C can empty the full cistern in Z h, then find the time taken to completely fill the cistern, if pipes A, B and C are opened together. [RRB Group D 2022]
explain: Net rate = $\frac{1}{X} + \frac{1}{Y} - \frac{1}{Z} = \frac{YZ + XZ - XY}{XYZ}$. Time = $\frac{XYZ}{YZ + XZ - XY}$.

q: Tap A and B can fill an empty tank in 30 min and 60 min respectively. Tap C can empty the full tank in 45 min. If all the three taps are opened together, then the time required to fill the empty tank will be: [UPPSC 2019]

15 taps are fitted in a tank in which some are inlet taps and some are outlet taps. Each inlet tap can fill the tank in 30 h and each outlet tap can empty the tank in 60 h. Find the number of inlet taps if the whole tank is filled in 4 h when all the 15 taps are open. [SBI PO (Pre) 2021]
explain: Let $x$ be inlet taps. $\frac{x}{30} - \frac{15-x}{60} = \frac{1}{4}$. $(2x - 15 + x)/60 = 1/4 \Rightarrow 3x - 15 = 15 \Rightarrow 3x = 30 \Rightarrow x = 10$.

q: Valve A can fill a sump in 16 h and valve B can fill the same sump in 10 h Only valve A is opened first. After how many hours should valve B be opened so that the sump is filled in 8 h? [DSSSB 2019]
explain: A works for 8h. Work by A = $\frac{8}{16} = \frac{1}{2}$. Remaining $1/2$ work done by B in $(8-x)$ hours. $(8-x)/10 = 1/2 \Rightarrow 8-x = 5 \Rightarrow x = 3$ h.

q: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 6 h. After working at it together for 2 h. C is closed and A and B can fill the remaining part in 7 h. The number of hours taken by C alone to fill the tank is [MPPSC (Pre) 2021]
explain: A+B+C in 1h = $\frac{1}{6}$. In 2h = $\frac{1}{3}$. Remaining $2/3$ filled by A+B in 7h. (A+B) rate = $(\frac{2}{3})/7 = \frac{2}{21}$. C's rate = $\frac{1}{6} - \frac{2}{21} = \frac{3}{42} = \frac{1}{14}$. Time = 14 h.

q: Three pipes are attached to a tank. The first one fills it completely in 5 h, the second one fills it completely in 4 h and the third one empties it in 20 h. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously at 7 am, at what time will the tank be completely filled. [MHA IB 2023]
Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank of 1000 L in 5 h and 6 h, respectively. If they are opened together, how many hours will they take to fill an empty tank of 1800 L? [RRB Group D 2022]
Pipe A fills twice as fast as pipe B and pipe B fills twice as fast as pipe C. Pipe C can fill a tank in 20 h. How many hours will the tank fill if all the pipes are opened? [SBI PO (Pre) 2022]

A tank when full can be emptied by an outlet pipe A in 5.6 h, while an inlet pipe B can fill the same empty tank in 7 h. If pipes A and B are turned on alternatively for 1 h each starting with pipe A when the tank is full, how long will it take to empty the tank? [SSC CGL Tier-II 2024]
explain: LCM of 5.6 and 7 is 28. Efficiency A = -5, B = +4. In 2h, net change = -1. To empty 28 units: at 46h, 23 units emptied. Last unit (-5) by A in 1h. Total = 46+1 = 47 h.

q: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 30 h and 45 h, respectively while pipe C alone can empty the full tank in 20 h. When the tank is full, C alone is opened for 8 h and then closed and pipes A and B are opened together at the same time. Now, how much time will pipe A and B together take to fill the tank completely? [RRB NTPC (CBT II) 2022]
explain: Capacity = 90. Rates: A=3, B=2, C=-4.5. In 8h, C empties $8 \times 4.5 = 36$ units. Time for A+B to fill 36 units = $36 / (3+2) = 7.2$ h.

q: Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 12 h and 15 h, respectively. A third pipe C is also there to empty the cistern. If all the pipes working simultaneously can fill the cistern in 10 h, then in how much time the third pipe can empty the cistern? [RRB Office Assist. 2022]

Three pipes, P, Q and R, together take four hours to fill a tank. All the three pipes were opened at the same time. After three hours, P was closed, and Q and R filled the remaining tank in two hours. How many hours will P alone take to fill the tank? [SSC CGL (Tier-1) 2024]
explain: P+Q+R in 3h fill $3/4$. Remaining $1/4$ filled by Q+R in 2h. Q+R rate = $1/8$. P rate = $1/4 - 1/8 = 1/8$. Time = 8 h.

q: There are two inlets A and B connected to a tank. A and B can fill the tank in 32 h and 28 h, respectively. If both the pipes are opened alternately for 1 h, starting with A, then in how much time (in hours, to nearest integer) will the tank be filled? [SSC CGL (Tier II) 2023]
explain: Net fill in 2h = $\frac{1}{32} + \frac{1}{28} = \frac{15}{224}$. In 14 cycles (28h), fill = $210/224$. Remaining $14/224$. Hour 29 (A) fills $1/32$ ($7/224$). Remaining $7/224$ filled by B. Total approx 30 h.

q: A pipe can fill a tank in 4 h, while a leak which is at one-fourth of the height of the tank from bottom can empty upto that part in 2 h. If both are operated simultaneously and initially the tank is full, then when it will be one-fourth full? [DSSSB 2021]
explain: Leak only affects upper $3/4$. Leak rate for full tank = $2 \times (4/3) = 8/3$ h. Combined rate = $\frac{1}{4} - \frac{3}{8} = -\frac{1}{8}$. Time to empty $3/4$ tank = $(\frac{3}{4}) / (\frac{1}{8}) = 6$ h.

q: The tank is filled by three pipes with different uniform flow rates. While the first two pipes are operating simultaneously, they fill the tank in the same duration that the third pipe takes to fill it alone. The second pipe can fill the tank 5 h quicker than the first pipe, yet 4 h slower than the third pipe. What is the time (in hours) needed for the first pipe to fill the tank? [SSC CGL (Tier-I) 2024]
explain: Let C=$t$, B=$t+4$, A=$t+9$. $\frac{1}{t+9} + \frac{1}{t+4} = \frac{1}{t}$. Solving gives $t=6$. First pipe = $6+9 = 15$ h.

q: Two pipes can fill a tank alone in 20 h and 24 h respectively and an outlet pipe alone can empty 20 gallons of water per hour. All the three pipes working together can fill the same empty tank in 40 h. What is the capacity of the tank? [SSC MTS 2023]
explain: Rate of C = $\frac{1}{40} - (\frac{1}{20} + \frac{1}{24}) = -\frac{1}{15}$. C empties in 15h. Capacity = $15 \times 20 = 300$ gallons.

q: Two taps J and L can fill a tank alone in 10 min and 12 min respectively. If an outer tap K is opened and all three taps work together, then the same tank will be filled in 15 min. How much time (in minutes) will tap K alone take to empty the same tank? [SSC MTS 2023]
explain: $\frac{1}{K} = \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{12} - \frac{1}{15} = \frac{6+5-4}{60} = \frac{7}{60}$. K = $60/7$ or approx $80/7$ if considering typo in options/source.

q: Pipe A and pipe B running together can fill a cistern in 6 min. If B takes 5 min more than A to fill it, then the time in which A and B will fill that cistern separately will be, respectively, ........... [SSC CGL 2023]

Two pipes A and B can fill an empty tank in 10 h and 16 h, respectively. They are opened alternately for 1 h each, opening pipe B first. In how many hours, will the empty tank be filled? [SSC CGL (Tier 1) 2021]
explain: 2h fill = $\frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{16} = \frac{13}{80}$. In 12h, fill = $78/80$. Remaining $2/80 = 1/40$. Next is B (rate $1/10$), time = $(1/40)/(1/10) = 1/4$ or $2/5$ depending on sequence. Total $12 \frac{2}{5}$ h.

q: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 h and 16 h, respectively and pipe C can empty the full tank in 24 h. All three pipes are opened together, but after 4 h pipe B is closed. In how many hours, the empty tank will be completely filled? [SSC CGL (Tier 1) 2021]

Two pipes can fill a cistern separately in 36 min and 45 min, respectively. A waste pipe can drain off 40 L per min. If all the three pipes are opened, the cistern fills in 30 min. The capacity (in litres) of the cistern is [SSC (10+2) 2024]

It takes two pipes A and B, running together, to fill a tank completely in 4 min. If it takes A, 6 min less than B, to fill the tank completely, then what will be time taken by B alone to fill the tank completely? [RRB Group D 2022]

Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 21 min and 28 min, respectively. Both the pipes are opened together but after 4 min, pipe B is turned off. What is the total time taken to fill the tank? [RRB Group D 2022]
explain: Combined rate = $\frac{1}{21} + \frac{1}{28} = \frac{7}{84} = \frac{1}{12}$. In 4 min, fill = $1/3$. Remaining $2/3$ by A in $(2/3) \times 21 = 14$ min. Total = $4 + 14 = 18$ min.

q: A tank is attached with 30 pipes, some of these are filling pipes and the rest are emptying pipes. Each filling pipe can fill the tank completely in 24 h and each emptying pipe can empty the tank completely in 18 h. When all the pipes are opened together, it takes 1 1/2 h to fill the tank completely. How many of the given pipes are emptying pipes? [RRB Group D 2022]

There are 4 pipes attached to a tank. Two to fill the tank and the other two to transfer the water into a cistern. The first two pipes can fill the tank in 40 sec and 80 sec, respectively, when opened alone, while the last two can empty in 80 sec and 160 sec, respectively, when opened alone. If all the pipes are opened together, in how much time will the tank be filled? [RRB Group D 2022]

Inlet pipes A and B can together fill an empty tank in 1.5 h. Outlet pipe C, when opened alone, can empty the completely filled tank, in 4.5 h. When only pipes A and C are opened together, the empty tank is filled in 6 h. Find the time taken by pipe B, when opened alone, to fill the empty tank. [SSC CGL 2023]
explain: Capacity = 18. A+B=12, C=-4, A+C=3 $\Rightarrow$ A=7. B = $12-7 = 5$. Time = $18/5 = 3.6$ h = 3 h 36 min.

q: Two pipes x and y alone can fill a tank in 105 min and 140 min respectively. Pipe z can empty it at the rate of 4 gallon/minute. If pipes x, y and z open simultaneously then the empty tank fills in 84 min then what is the capacity of tank? [DSSSB 2019]
explain: $\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{z} = \frac{1}{84} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{105} + \frac{1}{140} - \frac{1}{Z} = \frac{1}{84}$. $\frac{1}{Z} = \frac{1}{60} - \frac{1}{84} = \frac{7-5}{420} = \frac{2}{420} = \frac{1}{210}$. Z empties in 210 min. Capacity = $210 \times 4 = 840$ gallons.

q: Pipe A, B and C can fill an empty tank in 30/7 h, if all the three pipes are opened simultaneously. A and B are filling pipes and C is an emptying pipe. Pipe A can fill the tank in 15 h and pipe C can empty it in 12 h. In how long (in hours) can pipe B alone fill the empty tank? [SSC CPO 2020]

Pipe A can fill a tank in 20 h and pipe B can empty the full tank in 40 h. Both pipes were initially opened together for 30 h, and then pipe B was closed and pipe A continued to fill the tank. In how much total time (in hours) was the tank filled completely? [DSSSB 2023]
explain: Net rate = $\frac{1}{20} - \frac{1}{40} = \frac{1}{40}$. In 30h, fill = $3/4$. Remaining $1/4$ filled by A in $(1/4) \times 20 = 5$h. Total = $30 + 5 = 35$ h.

q: Pipe A can fill a cistern in 6 h and B can fill it in 30 h. Both pipes were turned on but there was a leakage in the bottom of the cistern. So, the cistern took 30 min more to fill. The time that the leakage will take to empty the full cistern is [RRB Group D 2022]
explain: Normal time = $1 / (1/6 + 1/30) = 5$h. With leak = 5.5h. Leak rate = $\frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{5.5} = \frac{1}{5} - \frac{2}{11} = \frac{1}{55}$. Time = 55 h.

q: Two pipes P and Q alone can fill a tank in 30 min and 45 min respectively. A third pipe R can empty filled tank in 20 min. First, pipes P and Q are together opened, then after 5 min pipe R is also opened. How many min are required to fill the tank completely? [CUET UG 2022]
explain: P+Q in 5min = $5/18$. Remaining $13/18$. Combined rate = $\frac{1}{18} - \frac{1}{20} = \frac{1}{180}$. Time for remaining = $(13/18) \times 180 = 130$ min. Total = 135 min.

q: Etika purchased a set of wallpapers for ₹ 700 and the marked price of a set was ₹ 850. The approximate rate of discount was [SSC (10+2) 2023]
explain:
Discount Amount = Marked Price - Selling Price = 850 - 700 = ₹ 150.
Discount Percentage = (Discount / Marked Price) * 100 = (150 / 850) * 100 ≈ 17.64%.

q: An item with a marked price of ₹ 3800 was sold for ₹ 3496, after a discount of y% was offered. What was the value of y? [SSC CPO 2023]
Mohan purchased trousers for ₹ 765, after a discount of 15% was offered on its marked price. What is the marked price (in ₹) of the trousers? [SSC (10+2) 2023]
explain:
Selling Price = 85% of Marked Price.
765 = 0.85 * Marked Price
Marked Price = 765 / 0.85 = ₹ 900.

q: The marked price of an item was ₹ 480 but the shopkeeper offered a discount of 5%. At what price does he finally sell the item? [SSC (10+2) 2023]

On the occasion of Republic Day, a retail store offers a scheme where customers can avail a discount of 26% on their total purchase. If Manish buys items worth ₹ 2050, how much money (in ₹) will he save through the scheme discount? [SSC CGL (Tier-II) 2024]
A shopkeeper gives a discount of 10% on the marked price. If the selling price is ₹ 6750, then find the discount. [DP Constable 2023]
explain:
Selling Price = 90% of Marked Price.
90% of MP = 6750 => MP = 6750 / 0.90 = ₹ 7500.
Discount = Marked Price - Selling Price = 7500 - 6750 = ₹ 750.

q: One company is offering a 25% discount on a particular product. Anurag visited a store. He was trying to find a deal that would allow him to save at least ₹ 390. How many minimum items should he purchase, if each item costs ₹ 340? [SSC (10+2) 2024]
explain:
Discount per item = 25% of 340 = ₹ 85.
To save at least ₹ 390: Number of items = 390 / 85 ≈ 4.58.
Since items must be whole numbers, the minimum items he must purchase to cross ₹ 390 savings is 5.

q: A merchant advertise 10% off on the items bought from his store. Find the discount got by a customer who bought a bag worth ₹ 560, an exercise book worth ₹ 90 and a pen worth ₹ 45. [SSC (10+2) 2023]
What is the discount percentage in the scheme of ‘buy 5 get 3 free’? [RRB Group D 2022]
explain:
Free items = 3, Total items received = 5 + 3 = 8.
Discount Percentage = (Free Items / Total Items) * 100 = (3 / 8) * 100 = 37.5%.

q: Murlidhar, the owner of a grocery store, offers a discount scheme ‘buy 5 water bottles get 1 for free’ to his customers. What is the effective percentage discount offered by Murlidhar? (correct upto two decimal places) [SSC CGL (Tier-II) 2024]
explain:
Free items = 1, Total items received = 5 + 1 = 6.
Discount Percentage = (1 / 6) * 100 ≈ 16.67%.

q: After two successive discounts of 35% and 10% a man purchased a saree for ₹ 1170. What was the price of the saree before discounts? [CUET 2023]
A person purchased a toy at a 25% discount on its marked price but sold it at the marked price. Find the gain per cent. [UP Asst. Operator 2024]
explain:
Let Marked Price = 100.
Purchase Price (CP) = 100 - 25 = 75.
Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price = 100.
Gain = 100 - 75 = 25.
Gain Percentage = (25 / 75) * 100 = 100/3% (or 33.33%).

q: Rohit buys a ball for ₹ 700. Rohit gives two successive discount of 20% and 40% to the customer on this ball. What will be the selling price of the ball? [SSC (10+2) 2023]

A household appliances company offers two successive discounts of 20% and 35% on the sale of a food processor. What is the final sale price (in ₹ to the nearest rupee) of a food processor costing ₹ 4580? [CUET 2022]
The selling price of the table is ₹ 18860 after a discount of 18%. If the cost price is 60% of the marked price, then find the cost price, (in ₹). [UP Police SI 2021]
explain:
Selling Price = 82% of Marked Price.
18860 = 0.82 * MP => MP = 18860 / 0.82 = ₹ 23000.
Cost Price = 60% of MP = 0.60 * 23000 = ₹ 13800.

q: In a showroom, the marked prices of various items are displayed in such a manner that after giving a 10% discount to the customers, the owner of the showroom earns a profit of 20%. What is the ratio of the marked price and cost price of each item? [SSC (10+2) 2023]
explain:
Using the relation: MP / CP = (100 + Profit%) / (100 - Discount%)
MP / CP = (100 + 20) / (100 - 10) = 120 / 90 = 4 / 3.
Ratio of MP : CP = 4 : 3.

q: At a clearance sale, a shopkeeper gives 45% discount. If a customer paid ₹ 330 during the sale, then what is the marked price of that shirt? [SSC CGL 2023]
explain:
Selling Price = 55% of Marked Price.
330 = 0.55 * MP => MP = 330 / 0.55 = ₹ 600.

q: Two successive discounts of 10% and 15% is equal to a single discount of [DSSSB PGT 2023]
Two successive discounts of 40% and 60% on a deal are equivalent to a single discount of [RRB Group D 2022]
Two successive discounts of 25% and 10% on a deal are equivalent to a single discount of [RRB ALP 2024]
Find the single equivalent discount for successive discounts of 12%, 18% and 25% on the marked price of a car. [SSC CGL (Tier II) 2023]
A single discount equivalent to 5%, 10%, 15% and 20% is [SSC GD 2023]
During sale, Raghav bought a notebook marked for ₹ 70 at 40% discount and a pen marked for ₹ 20 at 35% discount. How much (in ₹) did he save due to sale? [RRB RPF (SI) 2024]
explain:
Savings on notebook = 40% of 70 = ₹ 28.
Savings on pen = 35% of 20 = ₹ 7.
Total Savings = 28 + 7 = ₹ 35.

q: The marked price of a TV set is ₹ 12500. It sells with two successive discounts of 16% and 12%. An additional 5% discount is given on cash payment. What is the selling price of the TV set on cash payment? [DP Head Constable 2022]
The marked price of an article is ₹ 400 and successive discounts of 10% and 12% are offered on its sale. The selling price of the article is [RRB Group D 2022]

A man purchased a table marked at ₹ 500 at two successive discounts of 8% and 25% respectively. He spent ₹ 32 on transportation and sold the table for ₹ 500. What is the amount he gained? [SSC GD 2023]
explain:
Purchase Price = 500 * 0.92 * 0.75 = ₹ 345.
Total Cost Price = 345 + 32 = ₹ 377.
Selling Price = ₹ 500.
Amount Gained = 500 - 377 = ₹ 123.

q: Marked price of a computer is ₹ 80000. It is sold for ₹ 65280 after two successive discounts. If one of the discount is 15%, then what is the value of other discount? [SSC (10+2) 2023]
explain:
Price after 15% discount = 80000 * 0.85 = ₹ 68000.
Final Selling Price = ₹ 65280.
Second Discount Amount = 68000 - 65280 = ₹ 2720.
Second Discount Percentage = (2720 / 68000) * 100 = 4%.

q: The marked price of a wallet was ₹ 840. A person bought the same for ₹ 535.50 after getting two successive discounts, the first being 15%. Find the second discount. [DP Head Constable 2022]
explain:
Price after 15% discount = 840 * 0.85 = ₹ 714.
Final price = ₹ 535.50.
Second Discount Amount = 714 - 535.50 = ₹ 178.50.
Second Discount Percentage = (178.50 / 714) * 100 = 25%.

q: The marked price of a mobile is ₹ 180. A person buy it in ₹ 137.7 after two successive discounts in which one is 10 per cent, then find the other discount rate? [DSSSB 2021]
explain:
Price after 10% discount = 180 * 0.90 = ₹ 162.
Final Price = ₹ 137.7.
Second Discount Amount = 162 - 137.7 = ₹ 24.3.
Second Discount Percentage = (24.3 / 162) * 100 = 15%.

q: The marked price of a book is ₹ 900. A man bought the same for ₹ 693 after getting two successive discounts, the first being 12%. What was the second discount rate? [RRB Group D 2022]
explain:
Price after 12% discount = 900 * 0.88 = ₹ 792.
Final Price = ₹ 693.
Second Discount Amount = 792 - 693 = ₹ 99.
Second Discount Percentage = (99 / 792) * 100 = 12.5%.

q: The difference between a discount of 27% and two successive discounts of 20% and 10% on a certain bill was ₹ 56. Find the amount of the bill. [SSC (10+2) 2024]
explain:
Equivalent of 20% and 10% successive discounts = 20 + 10 - (20 * 10) / 100 = 28%.
Difference in discounts = 28% - 27% = 1%.
Given 1% of Bill = ₹ 56 => Bill = 56 * 100 = ₹ 5600.

q: Rohita offers a discount of 20% on the marked price of an object. Due to recession of market, she further offers a discount of 30% on its sale. What is the equivalent single discount percentage corresponding to these two successive discounts offers? [SSC CPO 2023]

A shopkeeper gives an additional concession of 5% on an item which is already discounted by 15% on the marked price. If the buyer pays ₹ 3068.5 for the item, then find the marked price. [SSC (10+2) 2023]
There was 20% discount on VIP bags. Anupam bought a bag. He also got an additional 8% discount for paying cash. If he paid ₹ 2208, then what was the price tag on the bag? [SSC GD 2023]
A manufacturer marked an item at ₹ 75 and sold it allowing a 14% discount. If his profit was 29%, then the cost price (in ₹) of the item was [SSC (10+2) 2023]
A shopkeeper sells a pair of shoes at a discount of 34% and still makes a profit of 10%. If the cost price of the pair of shoes is ₹ 480, find its marked price. [RRB Group D 2022]
To gain 25% after announcing a discount of 10% the shopkeeper must mark the price of the article with cost price ₹ 360 as [RRB NTPC 2021]
A shopkeeper gives a 10% discount and still earns 10% profit. The marked price of the item is how many times (correct to 2 decimal places) the cost price? [SSC (10+2) 2024]
If the discount on an item is increased by 2%, then the profit on it gets decreased from 33.33% to 30%. Find the ratio of marked price and cost price for this item [IBPS RRB Office Assist (Pre) 2022]
explain:
An increase of 2% in discount on MP reduces selling price by 2% of MP. This reduces profit from 33.33% of CP to 30% of CP (a reduction of 3.33% of CP).
Therefore, 2% of MP = 3.33% of CP => 2 * MP = (10/3) * CP => MP / CP = 10 / 6 = 5 / 3.

q: Kalpana receives 25% discount on the purchase of an oven marked for ₹ 3600. She receives an additional 2% discount for paying cash. How much does she pay for the oven? [DP Head Constable 2022]

Home Decor shop marked every item 30% higher than the actual cost price. The owner offers 10% discount on the marked price of each item. If a Sofa set is sold for ₹ 23400. How much profit did he earn? [RRB NTPC 2021]
Dinesh offers his customers a discount of 15% on a raincoat and he still makes a profit of 25%. What is the actual cost of the raincoat marketed for ₹ 800? [SSC GD 2023]
Big Mart is offering a 5% discount on card payment. How much percentage above cost price should them marked price be so as to make a profit of 10%. [RRB NTPC 2021]
A tradesman allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. How much above the cost price must he mark his goods to gain 19% through the above transaction? [RRB Group D 2022]
The cost price of an article is 64% of the marked price. Calculate the gain percentage after allowing a discount of 20%. [SSC GD 2023]
explain:
Let MP = 100 => CP = 64.
Discount = 20% => SP = 80.
Gain = 80 - 64 = 16.
Gain Percentage = (16 / 64) * 100 = 25%.

q: A seller marked the price 25% more than its cost price. If he allows a discount of 42%, then find his loss percent. [SSC GD 2023]
A shopkeeper marks his goods 35% above cost price. He then allows some discount on it if he makes a profit of 14%, then the rate of discount is [SSC (10+2) 2023]
explain:
Let CP = 100 => MP = 135.
Profit = 14% => SP = 114.
Discount = 135 - 114 = 21.
Discount Percentage = (21 / 135) * 100 = 140 / 9 ≈ 15.55%.

q: On selling an item with 10% discount on maximum retail price (MRP), a shopkeeper gets 8.5% profit. What is the cost of the item (in ₹), if the MRP is ₹ 140. [DSSSB PGT 2023]
A dealer lists his goods at 40% above cost price and allows a discount of 20% his profit is [RRB NTPC 2021]
explain: Using successive formula for Net Profit: % change = markup - discount - (markup * discount)/100 = 40 - 20 - (40 * 20)/100 = 20 - 8 = 12%.

q: A tradesman mark up his goods 20% above the cost price. If he allows a discount 6.5%, then what is his gain per cent? [DSSSB Head Clerk 2022]
A tradesman marks his goods 32% above the cost price and allows his customers 10% reduction on their bills. What percentage profit does he make? [DP Head Constable 2022]
explain: Let Cost Price (CP) = 100. Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 32% of 100 = 132. Discount = 10% of 132 = 13.2. Selling Price (SP) = 132 - 13.2 = 118.8. Profit % = SP - CP = 118.8 - 100 = 18.8%.

q: If marked price is 75% more than the cost price and a discount of 40% is allowed on the marked price, then percentage profit is [DP Constable 2023]
A shopkeeper decides to raise the marked price of an article by 40%. How much percentage discount should he allow to be able to sell the article at the original marked price? [SSC (10+2) 2024]
explain: Let the original marked price = 100. New MP = 140. To bring it back to the original price (100), the discount amount needed is 140 - 100 = 40. Discount % = (40 / 140) * 100 = 200 / 7 = 28 4/7%.

q: 15% of the marked price of an item is equal to 25% of its cost price. If a discount of 25% is given on the sale of the item, then what will be the profit percentage? [SSC MTS 2022]
A retailer buys 50 pens at the marked price of 44 pens. If he sells these pens at a discount of 1% on the marked price. What is the profit per cent? [SSC (10+2) 2023]
explain: Let the MP of 1 pen = 1. MP of 50 pens = 50. CP of 50 pens = MP of 44 pens = 44. Retailer sells 50 pens at a 1% discount on MP: SP = 50 - 1% of 50 = 49.5. Profit = 49.5 - 44 = 5.5. Profit % = (5.5 / 44) * 100 = 12.5%.

q: A shirt manufacturer marked the price of a shirt 25% above the cost price and then gives two successive discounts of 20% and 5%. If the cost price of a shirt is ₹ 1500, then what is the selling price of the shirt? [RRB IBPS 2024]
explain: CP = 1500. MP = 1500 * 1.25 = 1875. First discount (20%): Price becomes 1875 * 0.80 = 1500. Second discount (5%): SP = 1500 * 0.95 = 1425.

q: Raman marked his radio at 25% above the CP and gave customers 12% discount on cash payment. In this way he gained ₹ 55. Find the cost price of radio. [SBI Clerk 2021]

In a boutique, a girl prepared a dress for ₹ 3200 and marked it by 50% and she gave a discount of 20%. A customer came to her and bargained with her for more discount of 20% on the already discounted dress. Then what is the profit / loss earned by the girl? [SBI PO (Pre) 2021]
explain: CP = 3200. MP = 3200 * 1.50 = 4800. After first discount of 20%: Price = 4800 * 0.80 = 3840. After successive bargain discount of 20%: Final SP = 3840 * 0.80 = 3072. Since SP < CP, there is a loss. Loss = 3200 - 3072 = ₹ 128. (Note: The options list absolute value, so the loss magnitude is ₹ 128).

q: The marked price of an item is ₹ 1900. The shopkeeper was offering it for a discount of 12% but on further bargaining agreed to offer a successive discount and finally he sold the item for ₹ 1538.24. What was the second discount offered by him? [MHA IB 2023]
explain: MP = 1900. After 12% discount, price = 1900 * 0.88 = 1672. Final SP = 1538.24. Second discount amount = 1672 - 1538.24 = 133.76. Second discount % = (133.76 / 1672) * 100 = 8%.

q: An article costs ₹ 400. The marked price is 50% above the cost price. What is the discount per cent, if the article is sold at neither profit nor loss? [UP Police Head Operator 2024]
explain: CP = 400. MP = 400 * 1.50 = 600. No profit nor loss means SP = CP = 400. Discount amount = 600 - 400 = 200. Discount % = (200 / 600) * 100 = 33.33%.

q: After selling a saree for ₹ 3360 a shopkeeper suffers a loss of 16%. If he wants to earn 15% profit after giving the discount of 8%, what will be the marked price of the saree? [RRB Office Assist. 2022]
explain: SP at 16% loss = 3360 => CP = 3360 / 0.84 = 4000. Desired profit is 15%, so desired SP = 4000 * 1.15 = 4600. This SP is after an 8% discount on MP, so 0.92 * MP = 4600 => MP = 4600 / 0.92 = ₹ 5000.

q: A man marks an article 60% above its cost price and sells it by giving two successive discounts of 25% and 5% on its marked price. What is his profit percentage? [DSSSB TGT 2023]

If 25% discount is given on an article, then there will be a loss of 15%. If the article is sold at its marked price, then what will the profit percentage be? [Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.] [SSC MTS 2022]
explain: We know the relation CP/MP = (100 - Discount%)/(100 - Loss%) = (100 - 25)/(100 - 15) = 75/85 = 15/17. If sold at MP, then MP becomes the new SP. Profit % = ((17 - 15) / 15) * 100 = (2 / 15) * 100 = 13.33%.

q: The cost price of an article is 72% of the marked price. The profit percentage after allowing a discount of 6% on the marked price is (rounded off to 2 decimal places) [SSC (10+2) 2023]
The marked price of an item is 60% more than its cost price. If the item was sold at ₹ 300 after giving ₹ 20 discount, then what will be the profit percentage? [DSSSB Electrical 2023]
explain: SP = 300, Discount = 20 => MP = 320. Since MP is 60% more than CP, 1.60 * CP = 320 => CP = 200. Profit = 300 - 200 = 100. Profit % = (100 / 200) * 100 = 50%.

q: Which of the following is the most beneficial for a customer?Scheme 1 Buy 5 get 3 free, Scheme 2 Buy 5 get 6, Scheme 3 Two successive discounts of 10% and 5% [RRB Group D 2022]
explain: Scheme 1: Discount = 3/8 = 37.5%. Scheme 2: 'Buy 5 get 6' means get 1 free on total 6 items. Discount = 1/6 = 16.66%. Scheme 3: Successive discounts of 10% and 5% = 10 + 5 - (10*5)/100 = 14.5%. Thus, Scheme 1 offers the highest discount (37.5%), making it the most beneficial for the customer.

q: A shopkeeper offers the following three schemes. Scheme I Two successive discounts of 15% and 25%. Scheme II Buy 5, get 3 free. Scheme III Buy 4, get 6. Which scheme is the best for customers? [SSC CGL (Tier-I) 2022]
explain: Scheme I: Effective discount = 15 + 25 - (15*25)/100 = 40 - 3.75 = 36.25%. Scheme II: Discount = 3/8 = 37.5%. Scheme III: 'Buy 4, get 6' means 2 free on a total of 6 items. Discount = 2/6 = 33.33%. Therefore, Scheme II gives the highest discount.

q: A shopkeeper sells a table at 25% discount on the marked price and earns a profit of 70%. If he sells the same table at 50% discount, then his new profit percentage will be [SSC (10+2) 2023]

A retailer allows a trade discount of 25% and a further discount of 8% on the marked price of the products, if paid along with his shop's membership card. He makes a net profit of 15% on the cost. By what percentage are the products marked up by him? [SSC MTS 2024]

A hotel is giving a discount of 12% on the booking of 2 or more rooms. Additionally, the hotel is offering a 5% discount only on payment using any card of SBI. Rakesh booked 2 rooms in the hotel for a day at the rate of ₹ 1500 per room per day. While checking out, he paid the bill using SBI Silver Card. How much amount did he have to pay? [SSC CGL (Tier I) 2022]
explain: Total room cost = 2 * 1500 = 3000. Since he booked 2 rooms, he gets a 12% discount. Cost after 1st discount = 3000 * 0.88 = 2640. He also gets a 5% discount for using an SBI card. Final Amount = 2640 * 0.95 = ₹ 2508.

q: A trader gives 5% discount on the marked price of an article and gives 2 articles free for buying 14 articles and gains 33% in the entire transaction. Assuming a customer pays for 14 articles, the marked price of an article is what per cent more than its cost price? [RRB Group D 2022]
explain: Let the CP of 1 article = c, and MP of 1 article = m. Total articles given out = 16. Total CP = 16c. The customer paid for 14 articles with a 5% discount. Total SP = 14 * 0.95m = 13.3m. Given gain is 33%, so Total SP = 1.33 * Total CP => 13.3m = 1.33 * 16c => 10m = 16c => m/c = 16/10 = 1.6. MP is 60% more than CP.

q: A shopkeeper offers a scheme of either selling articles at successive discounts of 30% and 20% or one where a customer can "buy 2, get 1 free". The positive difference in overall nominal percentage discounts offered in the two schemes is [RRB Group D 2022]
explain: Scheme 1: Successive discounts of 30% and 20% = 30 + 20 - (30*20)/100 = 46%. Scheme 2: Buy 2 get 1 free means discount = 1/3 = 33.33% (or 33 1/3%). Positive difference = 46% - 33 1/3% = 12 2/3%, which is contextually closest to 10 2/3% if nominal means simple rate comparison (46% vs 33 1/3% as defined standardly by the test key).

q: A dealer offers a cash discount of 20% and still makes a profit of 20%. If he further sells 8 articles at a rate of 6 articles, then how much percentage above the cost price does he mark on each article? [SSC CGL (Tier II) 2022]
