explain: Let CP of 1 article = c, and MP of 1 article = m. Dealer sells 8 articles but charges for 6, giving a 20% cash discount on those 6. Total SP = 6 * 0.8m = 4.8m. Total items given = 8, so Total CP = 8c. He makes 20% overall profit, so Total SP = 1.2 * Total CP => 4.8m = 1.2 * 8c => 4.8m = 9.6c => m = 2c. Thus, MP is 100% above CP.

q: A discount of 10% is offered on the price of an article if the payment is made online. An additional discount of 5% is given to credit card holders. A person wishes to buy a watch priced at ₹ 60000 by paying online through credit card. How much does he need to pay (in ₹)? [SSC CGL (Tier II) 2022]
explain: Price = 60000. Online discount (10%): 60000 * 0.90 = 54000. Credit card discount (5%): 54000 * 0.95 = ₹ 51300.

q: A shopkeeper sells an item for ₹ 855.4 after giving two successive discounts of 90% and 75% on its marked price. Had he not given any discount, he would have earned a profit of 40%. What is the cost price (in ₹) of the item? [RPF (SI) 2024]

The marked price of an article is 40% more than its cost price. The shopkeeper gives a discount of 28.57% on marked price. On request, he gives another discount that was equal to 12.5% of the cost price. What was the approximate loss per cent of shopkeeper? [DSSSB Junior Steno 2021]
explain: Let CP = 100. Then MP = 140. Discount of 28.57% (which is 2/7) on MP: 140 * (2/7) = 40. Price after 1st discount = 140 - 40 = 100. Additional discount = 12.5% of CP = 12.5. Final SP = 100 - 12.5 = 87.5. Loss = CP - SP = 100 - 87.5 = 12.5. Loss % = 12.5%.

q: Raj sells a cricket bat of marked price ₹ 500 at a discount of 10% and gives a ball costing ₹ 10 free with each bat. Still, he makes a profit of 25%, the cost price of the bat is [IBPS Clerk (Pre) 2021]
explain: MP of bat = 500. Discount on bat = 10% of 500 = 50. Revenue from customer = 500 - 50 = 450. Total cost incurred by Raj = CP of bat + Cost of ball = CP + 10. Profit is 25%, so 1.25 * (CP + 10) = 450 => CP + 10 = 360 => CP = ₹ 352.

q: An article is sold at a discount of 25% and an additional discount of 28% is allowed on cash payment. If Ramendra purchased the article by paying ₹ 10800 in cash, then what was the marked price of the article? [SSC CPO 2023]

If the price of an item is increased by 70% and then allows a scheme discount of 5% and 20% on this marked price. If price is paid in cash and additional discount of 20% is allowed, then what is his gain percentage? [SSC CPO 2023]

The marked price of a trouser and a jacket is in the ratio of 1 : 3. The shopkeeper gives 20% discount on the trouser. If the total discount offered on both of them together is 30%, then what is the discount percentage offered on the jacket? [SSC (10+2) 2023]
explain: Let MP of trouser = 100 and jacket = 300. Total MP = 400. Total discount = 30% of 400 = 120. Discount on trouser = 20% of 100 = 20. Discount on jacket = 120 - 20 = 100. Discount % on jacket = (100 / 300) * 100 = 33.33%.

q: A shopkeeper sells in an item for ₹ 571.20 after giving two successive discounts of 20% and 15% on its marked price. Had he not given any discount, he would have earned a profit of 12%. What is the cost price (in ₹) of the item? [RRB Group D 2022]

A dealer marks his goods at 40% above the cost price. He sells 60% of the goods at the marked price giving 10% discount and the rest by giving 50% discount on the marked price. What is his overall profit/loss per cent? [SSC CGL (Tier II) 2020]
explain: Let total goods = 100 and CP of each = 1. Total CP = 100. MP of each = 1.4. SP of 60% goods (60 items) = 60 * 1.4 * 0.90 = 75.6. SP of 40% goods (40 items) = 40 * 1.4 * 0.50 = 28. Total SP = 75.6 + 28 = 103.6. Profit = 103.6 - 100 = 3.6%.

q: A trader gains 25% by selling an article with 20% discount on its marked price. If the cost price of the article increases by 30%, then how much discount (in %) should he offer on the same marked price to gain 15% of profit? [SSC CGL (Tier-II) 2022]

Trader A offers a discount of 25% on the marked price for cash purchase. Trader B offers a trade discount of 20% and a cash discount of 4% on the same article marked at the same price as that of Trader A. If the discount given by Trader A is ₹ 360 more than the discount given by Trader B, then what is the marked price of the item (in ₹)? [DP Head Constable 2023]
explain: Let MP = x. Discount by A = 25% of x = 0.25x. Scheme B effective discount = 20 + 4 - (20*4)/100 = 23.2%. Discount by B = 23.2% of x = 0.232x. Difference = 0.25x - 0.232x = 0.018x. Given 0.018x = 360 => x = 360 / 0.018 = ₹ 20000.

q: A dishonest dealer marks up his goods by 50% and then gives a discount of 20% on the marked price. Apart from this, he uses a faulty balance which reads 1kg for 900 gm. What is his net profit percentage (rounded off to the nearest integer)? [SSC CGL 2023]
explain: Markup and discount effective multiplier = 1.50 * 0.80 = 1.20 (20% profit on nominal price). Due to weight fraud, he charges for 1000g but only gives 900g. Overall ratio SP/CP = (1.20) * (1000 / 900) = 1.2 * 10/9 = 12/9 = 4/3. Profit % = ((4 - 3) / 3) * 100 = 33.33% ≈ 33%.

q: After allowing a discount of 15% on cost price of on one article, its selling price becomes equal to the selling price of another article after allowing a discount of 25% on another article. If the sum of cost prices of both article is ₹ 640, then find the selling price of each article. [SSC CGL (Tier II) 2020]

Rohan purchased an item for which there was a 13.5% discount offered on the part of the payment made in cash and a 6.25% surcharge on the part of the payment made through a credit card. If Rohan would have paid the entire amount in cash he would have paid ₹ y for the item. But he actually had to pay ₹ 40964 in all for the item, out of which ₹ 29064 was paid in cash. What is the value of y? [MHA IB 2024]
explain: Let total marked value of cash part be C and card part be K. Cash paid = C * (1 - 0.135) = 0.865C = 29064 => C = 29064 / 0.865 = 33600. Card paid = 40964 - 29064 = 11900. Card part with surcharge = K * 1.0625 = 11900 => K = 11900 / 1.0625 = 11200. Total marked price of item = C + K = 33600 + 11200 = 44800. If he paid fully in cash, he would get 13.5% discount overall: y = 44800 * (1 - 0.135) = 44800 * 0.865 = ₹ 35700.

q: The marked price of an article is ₹ 1500. If two successive discounts each of x% on the marked price is equal to a single discount of ₹ 587.40, then what will be the selling price of the article if a single discount of x% is given on the marked price? [SSC CGL (Tier II) 2019]
explain: Final SP after two discounts = 1500 - 587.40 = 912.60. Formulating equation: 1500 * (1 - x/100)^2 = 912.60 => (1 - x/100)^2 = 912.60 / 1500 = 0.6084. Taking square root: 1 - x/100 = 0.78 => x = 22%. If single discount of 22% is given, SP = 1500 * 0.78 = ₹ 1170.

q: A 900 m long train crosses a 1200 m long platform completely in 70 sec. What is the speed of the train?
explain: Total distance to be covered = (900 + 1200) m = 2100 m. Time taken = 70 sec. Speed = Distance / Time = 2100 / 70 = 30 m/s = 30 * (18/5) km/h = 108 km/h.

q: A train is moving at a uniform speed of 80 km/h. How much distance is covered by the train in 30 min?
explain: Given, speed of train = 80 km/h. Time = 30 min = 30/60 = 1/2 h. Distance = Time * Speed = (1/2) * 80 = 40 km.

q: Two trains, one 125 m and the other 375 m long are running in opposite directions on parallel tracks, at the speed of 81 km/h and 63 km/h, respectively. How much time will they take to cross each other?
A train 700 m long is running at the speed of 72 km/h. If it crosses a tunnel in 1 min, then the length of the tunnel is
explain: Speed = 72 * (5/18) = 20 m/s. Let the length of tunnel be x m. Then, (700 + x) / 20 = 60 => 700 + x = 1200 => x = 500 m.

q: Find the time taken by a train 750 m long to cross a platform twice its length at a speed of 81 km/h.
explain: Length of train is 750 m. Length of platform = 2 * 750 = 1500 m. Speed of train = 81 km/h = 81 * (5/18) = 45/2 m/s. Time taken to cross platform = (750 + 1500) / (45/2) = (2250 * 2) / 45 = 100 sec.

q: A 480 m long train takes 16 sec to pass a pole. How long will it take to pass a platform that is 900 m long?
explain: Speed of the train = Length of the train / Time taken to cross a pole = 480 / 16 = 30 m/s. Time = Total distance / Speed = (480 + 900) / 30 = 1380 / 30 = 46 sec.

q: Two goods trains 132 m and 108 m in length are running towards each other on parallel tracks. The first train is running at a speed of 32 km/h and the second at a speed of 40 km/h. How much time will they take to cross each other after meeting?
explain: Length of trains are 132 m and 108 m and speed of trains are 32 km/h and 40 km/h. Time required to cross each other = (132 + 108) / [(32 + 40) * (5/18)] = 240 / [72 * (5/18)] = 240 / 20 = 12 sec.

q: A train passes two bridges of length 600 m and 200 m in 80 sec and 40 sec respectively. The length of the train is
explain: Let length of train be L and speed be s m/s. From bridge 1: (L + 600) / 80 = s. From bridge 2: (L + 200) / 40 = s. Equating both: (L + 600) / 80 = (L + 200) / 40 => L + 600 = 2L + 400 => L = 200 m.

q: A train 525 m long running at a speed of 103 km/h overtake another train which is 425 m long running at a speed of 73 km/h in the same direction. Find the time taken by the faster train to overtake the slower train [in sec].
explain: Total length of train = 525 + 425 = 950 m. Relative speed of both trains = 103 - 73 = 30 km/h = 30 * (5/18) = 25/3 m/s. Required time taken = 950 / (25/3) = (950 * 3) / 25 = 114 sec.

q: Two trains of lengths 257.5 m and 272.5 m, travelling in opposite directions crossed each other in 15.9 sec. What is their approximate combined speed per hour?
explain: Total distance travelled by both trains to cross each other = 257.5 + 272.5 = 530 m. Combined speed = (530 / 15.9) * (18/5) km/h = 120 km/h (approx).

q: Two trains with a speed of 80 km/h and 120 km/h, respectively, are 500 km apart and face each other. Find the distance between them 10 min before crossing.
explain: Required distance between the trains = relative speed * remaining time = (80 + 120) * (10/60) = 200 * (1/6) = 33.33 km.

q: At 46 km/h and 36 km/h, two trains of equal length are travelling in the same direction on parallel lines. What is the length of each train, if the quicker train passes the slower train in 36 sec?
explain: Let the length of each train be x m. Relative speed = 46 - 36 = 10 km/h = 10 * (5/18) m/s. Distance = Speed * Time => 2x = 10 * (5/18) * 36 => 2x = 100 => x = 50 m.

q: Two trains of equal length are running on parallel lines in the same direction at speeds of 51 km/h and 42 km/h. The faster train passes the slower train in 16 sec. The length of each train is
explain: Let the length of each train = x m. Relative speed = 51 - 42 = 9 km/h = 9 * (5/18) m/s. Distance = Speed * Time => 2x = 9 * (5/18) * 16 => 2x = 40 => x = 20 m.

q: Two trains started from a station, at the same time in the same direction, at speeds of 90 km/h and 80 km/h. What will be the distance between the two trains after 5 h?
explain: Relative speed = 90 - 80 = 10 km/h. Distance between two trains after 5 h = 5 * 10 = 50 km.

q: A and B are two stations 420 km apart. A train starts from A at 11 am and travels towards B at the speed of 70 km/h. Another train starts from B at 12 noon and travels towards A at the speed of 30 km/h. At what time do they meet?
explain: By 12 noon, train from A covers 70 km. Remaining distance = 420 - 70 = 350 km. Relative speed = 70 + 30 = 100 km/h. Time taken to meet from 12 noon = 350 / 100 = 3.5 hours. Meeting time = 12 noon + 3.5 h = 3:30 pm.

q: A goods train 350 m long passes through a tunnel of length 1250 m in 80 sec. What is the speed of the train?
If a train 130 m long takes 6(1/2) sec to cross a man, who is walking at 12 km/h in the same direction in which the train is going, then the speed of the train (in km/h) is
explain: Let the speed of train = S km/h. Distance = Relative speed * Time => 130 = (S - 12) * (5/18) * (13/2) => 130 = (S - 12) * (65/36) => S - 12 = 72 => S = 84 km/h.

q: The distance between P and Q is 720 km. A train leaves P at 6 am and runs at a speed of 20 m/s. The train stops on the way for 1 h 30 min. At what time train will reach at Q?
explain: Speed = 20 m/s = 20 * (18/5) = 72 km/h. Running time = 720 / 72 = 10 hours. Total time = 10 h + 1 h 30 min = 11 h 30 min. Arrival time = 6:00 am + 11 h 30 min = 5:30 pm.

q: A train starts from a place S at 10:00 am and arrives at another place T at 2:30 pm on the same day. If the speed of the train is 40 m/s, then what will be the distance covered by the train?
explain: Speed = 40 m/s = 40 * (18/5) = 144 km/h. Time taken = 10:00 am to 2:30 pm = 4.5 h = 9/2 h. Distance = 144 * (9/2) = 648 km.

q: The distance between two stations A and B is 200 km. A train runs from A to B at a speed of 75 km/h, while another train runs from B to A at a speed of 85 km/h. What will be the distance between the two trains (in km) 3 min before they meet?
explain: Relative speed = 75 + 85 = 160 km/h. Distance covered in 3 min before meeting = Relative Speed * Time = 160 * (3/60) = 8 km.

q: The speed of a train is 78 km/h. It crosses a tunnel in 45 sec and overtakes a person walking at a speed of 6 km/h in the same direction in 15 sec. The length (in metre) of the tunnel is
explain: Speed of train = 78 km/h = 78 * (5/18) = 65/3 m/s. Speed of person = 6 km/h = 6 * (5/18) = 5/3 m/s. Relative speed with person = 65/3 - 5/3 = 20 m/s. Length of train = Relative speed * time = 20 * 15 = 300 m. For tunnel: (300 + Tunnel) = Speed * time = (65/3) * 45 = 975 m => Tunnel = 975 - 300 = 675 m.

q: Two trains of equal length are running on parallel lines in the same direction at speeds of 46 km/h and 36 km/h. The faster train passes the slower train in 36 sec. The relative speed of these two trains (in m/s) is
explain: Relative speed in same direction = 46 - 36 = 10 km/h = 10 * (5/18) = 50/18 = 25/9 m/s.

q: Two trains are running in opposite directions. They cross a man standing on a platform in 28 sec and 10 sec respectively. They cross each other in 24 sec. What is the ratio of their speeds?
explain: Let speeds be x and y. Lengths are 28x and 10y. Time to cross each other = (28x + 10y) / (x + y) = 24 => 28x + 10y = 24x + 24y => 4x = 14y => x/y = 14/4 = 7:2.

q: Two trains 180 m and 200 m long are running in opposite directions at the speed 40 km/h and 50 km/h respectively. In how much time will they cross each other?
explain: Total distance = 180 + 200 = 380 m. Relative speed = 40 + 50 = 90 km/h = 90 * (5/18) = 25 m/s. Time = 380 / 25 = 15.2 sec ≈ 15 sec.

q: The ratio between the speeds of two trains is 7:8. If the second train runs 400 km in 4 h, then find the speed of the first train.
explain: Speed of second train = 400 / 4 = 100 km/h. Since ratio is 7:8, speed of first train = (100 / 8) * 7 = 87.5 km/h.

q: Two trains each 250 m in length, are running on parallel lines in opposite directions at speeds of 90 km/h and 60 km/h respectively. In how many seconds will they cross each other completely?
Two trains, 140 m and 120 m in length, are running in the same direction at the speed of 60 km/h and 78 km/h, respectively. In how much time will they completely cross each other?
explain: Total distance = 140 + 120 = 260 m. Relative speed = 78 - 60 = 18 km/h = 18 * (5/18) = 5 m/s. Time = 260 / 5 = 52 sec.

q: Trains A and B start at the same time. Train A travels at the speed of 50 km/h from station P to station Q and train B travels at the speed of 70 km/h from station Q to station P. They cross each other after 1 h 20 min. What is the distance (in km) between station P and station Q?
explain: Relative speed = 50 + 70 = 120 km/h. Time = 1 h 20 min = 4/3 h. Distance = 120 * (4/3) = 160 km.

q: Two trains start running at the same time. Train A travels from city M to city N while traveling at an average speed of 54 km/h, while train B travels from city N to city M. The distance between the two cities is 960 km. If both the trains cross each other after 8 h, then find the average speed (in km/h) of train B?
explain: Combined relative speed = 960 / 8 = 120 km/h. Speed of train B = Combined speed - Speed of train A = 120 - 54 = 66 km/h.

q: Two trains travelling in the same direction at 40 km/h and 22 km/h cross each other completely in 1 min. If the length of the first train is 125 m what is the length of the second train?
explain: Relative speed = 40 - 22 = 18 km/h = 18 * (5/18) = 5 m/s. Total distance covered in 1 min (60 sec) = 5 * 60 = 300 m. Length of second train = 300 - 125 = 175 m.

q: Two trains 200 m and 150 m long are running on parallel tracks at the rates of 40 km/h and 45 km/h respectively. In how much time will they cross each other if they are running in the same direction?
explain: Total length = 200 + 150 = 350 m. Relative speed = 45 - 40 = 5 km/h = 5 * (5/18) = 25/18 m/s. Time taken = 350 / (25/18) = 14 * 18 = 252 sec.

q: A train passes a man, going in opposite direction, in 12 sec and the speed of the man is 10 km/h. If the speed of the train is 62 km/h, then what is the length (in m) of the train?
explain: Relative speed = 62 + 10 = 72 km/h = 72 * (5/18) = 20 m/s. Length of train = Speed * Time = 20 * 12 = 240 m.

q: Train A running with the speed of 36 km/h crosses a pole in 20 sec. Another train B whose length is 100 m more than length of train A is running with the speed of 18 km/h. Find the time taken by train B to cross a platform of length 500 m.
explain: Speed of train A = 36 km/h = 10 m/s. Length of A = 10 * 20 = 200 m. Length of B = 200 + 100 = 300 m. Speed of B = 18 km/h = 5 m/s. Time for B to cross platform = (300 + 500) / 5 = 800 / 5 = 160 sec.

q: A 360 m long train running at the speed of 108 km/h crosses another train running in the opposite direction at the speed of 90 km/h in 12 sec. What is the length (in m) of the other train?
explain: Relative speed = 108 + 90 = 198 km/h = 198 * (5/18) = 55 m/s. Total distance = 55 * 12 = 660 m. Length of other train = 660 - 360 = 300 m.

q: The length of a train and that of a platform are equal. If, with a speed of 150 km/h, the train crosses the platform in 1 min, then the length of the train is
explain: Speed = 150 km/h = 150 * (5/18) = 750/18 m/s. Time = 1 min = 60 sec. Total distance = (750/18) * 60 = 2500 m. Since train and platform lengths are equal, length of train = 2500 / 2 = 1250 m.

q: A train crosses a one km long bridge in one minute and a 750 m long tunnel in 50 sec. Assuming that the train is running at a uniform speed, what is its speed?

Two trains start from P and Q. respectively, at the same time and run towards each other at a speed of 40 km/h and 30 km/h, respectively. By the time they meet, the first train has covered 80 km more than the other train. Find the distance between P and Q.
explain: Let the time they meet be t hours. Difference in distance = 40t - 30t = 80 => 10t = 80 => t = 8 hours. Distance between P and Q = Total relative distance = (40 + 30) * 8 = 70 * 8 = 560 km.

q: Two trains start at the same time from two stations and proceed towards each other at speeds of 90 km/h and 70 km/h, respectively. When they meet, it is found that first train has travelled 140 km more than the other. What is the distance (in km) between the two stations?
explain: Difference in speed = 90 - 70 = 20 km/h. Time taken to meet = 140 / 20 = 7 hours. Total distance between the two stations = (90 + 70) * 7 = 160 * 7 = 1120 km.

q: Two trains, P and Q are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions with lengths of 110 m and 140 m, respectively. Train P is running at a speed of 70 km/h and took 5 sec to cross train Q. The speed of train Q is
explain: Total length = 110 + 140 = 250 m. Relative speed = 250 / 5 = 50 m/s = 50 * (18/5) = 180 km/h. Speed of Q = Relative speed - Speed of P = 180 - 70 = 110 km/h.

q: A train crosses a 400 m long platform in 50 sec. It crosses another 600 m long platform in 60 sec. What are the length and the speed of the train?

Places A and B are 396 km apart. train X leaves from A and B and train Y leaves from B for A at the same time on the same day on parallel tracks. Both trains meet after 5(1/2) h. The speed of Y is 10 km/h more than that of X. What is the speed (in km/h) of train Y?
explain: Relative speed = 396 / 5.5 = 72 km/h. Given Y = X + 10 => X + Y = 72 => 2X + 10 = 72 => 2X = 62 => X = 31 km/h. Speed of Y = 31 + 10 = 41 km/h.

q: Excluding stoppage stations, the speed of a train is 60 km/h and including stoppage stations it travels at a speed of 45 km/h. For how many minutes does the train stop per hour?
explain: Stoppage time per hour = (Speed excluding stoppage - Speed including stoppage) / Speed excluding stoppage = (60 - 45) / 60 = 15/60 = 1/4 hour = 15 minutes.

q: A train passes a platform in 36 sec and a man standing on the platform in 20 sec. If the speed of the train is 54 km/h, what is the length of the platform?
explain: Speed = 54 km/h = 54 * (5/18) = 15 m/s. Length of train = Speed * time to cross man = 15 * 20 = 300 m. Length of train + platform = 15 * 36 = 540 m. Length of platform = 540 - 300 = 240 m.

q: A train crosses a telegraph post and a bridge of length 300 m in 10 sec and 20 sec, respectively. Find the speed of the train.
explain: The train takes 20 - 10 = 10 sec to cover the bridge length of 300 m. Speed = 300 / 10 = 30 m/s = 30 * (18/5) = 108 km/h.

q: A train travels 50% faster than a bus. Both start from Karnal at the same time and reach Panipat 75 km away at the same time. On the way, however, the train lost about 12.5 minutes while stopping at the stations. The speed of the bus is
A train 400 m long running at 64 km/h crosses a man sitting in another train 720 m long running at 80 km/h in the opposite direction. Find the time taken by the second train to cross the man.
explain: Relative speed = 64 + 80 = 144 km/h = 144 * (5/18) = 40 m/s. To cross a man sitting in the 400 m train, the 720 m train needs to cover its own length. Time = 720 / 40 = 18 sec.

q: The distance between two stations A and B is 100 km. A train leaves A at 7:00 am and travels towards B at 20 km/h. Another train leaves B at 8:00 am and travels towards A at 25 km/h. At what time will they meet?
explain: By 8:00 am, train A covers 20 km. Remaining distance = 100 - 20 = 80 km. Relative speed = 20 + 25 = 45 km/h. Time to meet = 80 / 45 = 16/9 h = 1 h 47 min. Meeting time = 8:00 am + 1 h 47 min = 9:47 am.

q: The length of train A is twice the length of train B. When running in opposite directions, they pass each other in 18 sec. If their speeds are 93 km/h and 51 km/h respectively, how much time (in sec) will train A take to cross a bridge 605 m long?
explain: Relative speed = 93 + 51 = 144 km/h = 40 m/s. Total distance = 40 * 18 = 720 m. Given A = 2B => 3B = 720 => B = 240 m, A = 480 m. Speed of A = 93 km/h = 93 * (5/18) = 155/6 m/s. Time to cross bridge = (480 + 605) / (155/6) = 1085 * 6 / 155 = 42 sec.

q: The length of train A is half of train B. Train A passes a 100 m platform in 5 sec and train B passes a 100 m platform in 6 sec. If the speeds of A and B are in the ratio 2:3, find the length of train B.
explain: Let B = x, A = x/2. Speed A = 2P, Speed B = 3P. 2P = (x/2 + 100)/5 => 20P - x = 200. 3P = (x + 100)/6 => 18P - x = 100. Subtracting the equations: 2P = 100 => P = 50. Substituting P: 18(50) - x = 100 => 900 - x = 100 => x = 800 m.

q: The speed of a slower train is 28 m/s and a faster train is 144 km/h. The length of the faster train is twice that of the slower train. If they cross each other in 72 sec while travelling in the same direction, what is the length of the faster train?
explain: Speed of faster train = 144 * (5/18) = 40 m/s. Let slower train length be x, faster be 2x. Relative speed = 40 - 28 = 12 m/s. Time = 72 sec => 3x / 12 = 72 => x = 288 m. Length of faster train = 2x = 576 m.

q: An express train travels at an average speed of 100 km/h, stopping for 3 minutes after every 75 km. How long will it take to reach a destination 600 km away?
explain: Running time = 600 / 100 = 6 hours = 360 min. Number of stoppages = 600 / 75 = 8. Since the 8th stoppage is the final destination, it stops 7 times on the way. Stoppage time = 7 * 3 = 21 min. Total time = 360 + 21 = 381 min.

q: A train starts from station X at a certain speed and reaches station Y in 10 hours. Another train B leaves station X four hours after train A and reaches station Y at the same time as train A. Find the total time taken by train B to cover the distance between X and Y.
explain: Let distance be d. Train A's speed = d/10. Distance covered by A in 4 hours = 4 * (d/10) = 2d/5. Remaining distance = 3d/5. This remaining distance is covered by train B in 4 hours because it catches up at Y. Time taken by B for total distance d = 4 * (5/3) = 20/3 = 6.67 hours.

q: A train covers a distance of 12 km in 25 min. If its speed is decreased by 5 km/h, what will be the time taken to cover the same distance?

Train P running at 70 km/h completely overtakes train Q 170 m long running at 56 km/h in the same direction in 90 sec. How much time will train P take to completely cross train R of length 220 m running in the opposite direction at 74 km/h?
explain: Relative speed with Q = 70 - 56 = 14 km/h = 14 * (5/18) = 70/18 m/s. Total distance = (Lp + 170) = (70/18) * 90 = 350 => Lp = 180 m. Relative speed with R = 70 + 74 = 144 km/h = 40 m/s. Time to cross R = (180 + 220) / 40 = 400 / 40 = 10 sec.

q: Two trains of lengths 150 m and 250 m run on parallel lines. When they run in the same direction, they take 20 sec to cross each other and, when they run in the opposite direction, they take 5 sec to cross each other. What is the speed of the two trains?
explain: Let speeds be x and y. Total length = 150 + 250 = 400 m. Same direction: x - y = 400 / 20 = 20 m/s. Opposite direction: x + y = 400 / 5 = 80 m/s. Solving these: x = 50 m/s = 50 * (18/5) = 180 km/h; y = 30 m/s = 30 * (18/5) = 108 km/h.

q: A sum of money is divided among A, B, C in the ratio 3:2:5, respectively. If the share of C is ₹300 more than B then how much more money will A get than B?
explain: Let the shares of A, B, and C be 3x, 2x, and 5x. Given: 5x - 2x = 300 => 3x = 300 => x = 100. Difference between A and B: 3x - 2x = x = ₹100.

q: Giri and Kamal invested their capitals in a business in the ratio 5:7, respectively. If ₹1728 was the total money invested in the business, what is Giri's share in the business?
explain: Let Giri and Kamal’s shares be 5x and 7x. 5x + 7x = 1728 => 12x = 1728 => x = 144. Giri’s share: 5 * 144 = ₹720.

q: Profit of ₹29120 is divided among A, B and C so that A's share is 2(1/2) times B's and B's share is 1(1/5) times C. Find B's share.
explain: Let C's share be x, then B's is 6/5x and A's is 5/2 * 6/5x = 3x. Ratio A:B:C = 15:6:5. Total: 26x = 29120 => x = 1120. B’s share: 6 * 1120 = ₹6720.

q: X, Y and Z are partners in a Law Firm. During a particular year X received one-fourth of the profit, Y received one-third of the profit and Z received the remaining ₹20000. How much did Y receive?
explain: Let total profit = a. Z’s share = a - a/4 - a/3 = 5a/12. 5a/12 = 20000 => a = 48000. Y’s profit: 48000/3 = ₹16000.

q: Karthick and Balaji enter into partnership with their capitals in the ratio 5:6. At the end of 8 months, Karthick withdraws his capital. If they receive the profits in the ratio of 5:9, then how long was Balaji's capital used?
explain: Investment ratio = 5:6; Time ratio = 8:x. (5 * 8) / (6 * x) = 5/9 => 30x = 360 => x = 12.

q: Manan invested ₹76000 in a business. After few months, Vivek joined him with ₹57000. At the end of the year, the total profit was divided between them in the ratio 2:1. After how many months did Vivek join the business?

explain: Investment ratio A:B:C = 9:18:21 = 3:6:7. B’s share: 6x = 759 => x = 126.5. Total profit: 16x = 16 * 126.5 = ₹2024.

A and B invest in a business in the ratio of 7:8 for same time. If 7% of the total profit goes to charity and A's share in profit is ₹12600, then what is the total amount of profit earned?
explain: A’s profit 12600 (7 parts) => Total profit (15 parts) = 27000. Including charity: 27000 * 100/93 = ₹29032.25.

q: Person A started a business by investing ₹65000. After a few months, B joined him by investing ₹50000. Three months after the joining of B, C joined the two with an investment of ₹55000. Anu, Taru and Daksh started a business. Taru invested 1/6 of the total money, while investments of Anu and Daksh are equal. If the profit on the end of the year is ₹7200, find the difference between the profit of Taru and Daksh?
A invested ₹4500 in a business and after some time B also joined him and invested ₹4800. At the end of year B received ₹4400 profit out of ₹9900. After how much time did B join the business?
explain: Profit ratio A:B = 5500:4400 = 5:4. (4500 * 12) / (4800 * x) = 5/4 => x = 9 months. Joined after = 12 - 9 = 3 months.

q: A, B and C jointly started a business in which A invested ₹7000 for 12 months, B invested ₹8000 for 10 months and C invested ₹12000 for 6 months. A was the working member for which he received 20% of the profits as his remuneration. The total profit earned at the end of one year was ₹14750. What is C's share (in ₹) in the profit?
explain: Profit ratio = 21:20:18. After 20% remuneration, 59 units = 11800. C’s share = 18 * 200 = ₹3600.

q: A started the business with the investment of ₹36000. B and C joined him with some investments after 3 and 6 months. The profit is divided in the ratio of 2:3:5 at the end of the year. Find the difference between the investment made by B and C in the business?

R, S and T started a business by investing ₹25000, ₹15000 and ₹30000 respectively. If the total profit earned is ₹58800 and it is decided that one-third of the profit will be divided into their investment ratio and rest of the amount will be invested in another work, then what is the share of T?
explain: Investment ratio R:S:T = 5:3:6. 1/3 profit = 19600. T’s share = 6/14 * 19600 = ₹8400.

In what ratio must a grocer mixes two varieties of pulses costing 60 and 75 per kg, respectively, so as to get a mixture worth 65 per kg? [SSC(10+2)2024]
explain:
According to the rule of alligation, we have two varieties costing ₹60 and ₹75, and the mean price is ₹65.

Cost of variety 1 = 60
Cost of variety 2 = 75
Mean price = 65

By alligation components:
Cheaper identity: (75 - 65) = 10
Dearer identity: (65 - 60) = 5

Required ratio = 10 : 5 = 2 : 1.

q: 10 kg of superior quality of rice is mixed with 5 kg of inferior quality of rice. The prices of superior quality and inferior quality rice are 85 and 46, respectively. Find the average price per kg of the mixture. [SSC GD 2023]
explain:
Total price of superior quality rice = 10 * 85 = ₹850
Total price of inferior quality rice = 5 * 46 = ₹230
Total quantity of rice = 10 + 5 = 15 kg

Average price of the mixture = (850 + 230) / 15 = 1080 / 15 = ₹72.

q: A certain quantity of a 35% sugar solution is mixed with the 8 L of a 48% sugar solution to obtain a 40% sugar solution. How many litres of the 35% sugar solution was there in the mixture? [RRB NTPC 2022]
explain:
Using the alligation method:
Percentage of Type 1 = 35%
Percentage of Type 2 = 48%
Target percentage = 40%

By alligation rule:
Ratio of Type 1 to Type 2 = (48 - 40) : (40 - 35) = 8 : 5

Given that Type 2 solution = 8 L
5 units = 8 L => 1 unit = 8/5 L

Therefore, quantity of 35% solution (8 units) = 8 * (8 / 5) = 64 / 5 = 12.8 L.

q: A milkman mixed some water with milk to gain 25% by selling the mixture at the cost price. The ratio of water and milk, respectively, in the mixture is: [HCET 2022]
explain:
Let the Cost Price (CP) of 1 L of pure milk be ₹100.
Since he gains 25% by selling the mixture at the cost price, the effective CP of the mixture to him is reduced.

To gain 25% by selling at CP, the ratio of profit to cost must be 25% : 100% = 1 : 4.
Since profit comes entirely from the added water, the ratio of water to milk in the mixture is 1 : 4.

q: A sample of milk from a vessel contains 4% water. What quantity of pure milk should be added to 8 L of milk in the vessel to reduce the water content to 2%? [RRB NTPC 2021]
explain:
Initial quantity of the sample = 8 L
Water content = 4% of 8 L = 0.32 L

Let x litres of pure milk be added. The total volume becomes (8 + x) L.
The quantity of water remains the same (0.32 L) but now represents 2% of the total volume.

(8 + x) * 2% = 0.32
(8 + x) * 0.02 = 0.32
8 + x = 16
x = 8 L.

q: 6 kg of 48 per kg rice is mixed with 3 kg of another variety of rice to get a mixture costing 60 per kg. What is the price per kg of another variety rice in the mixture? [RRB Group D 2022]
explain:
Let the cost of the second variety of rice be ₹x/kg.

Quantity of variety 1 = 6 kg
Quantity of variety 2 = 3 kg
Ratio of quantities = 6 : 3 = 2 : 1

Using the formula for weighted average:
(6 * 48 + 3 * x) / (6 + 3) = 60
288 + 3x = 540
3x = 252
x = 84

Hence, the price of the other variety is ₹84/kg.

q: To make idlis, if you take two parts rice and one part urad dal, what percentage of such a mixture would be rice and what percentage would be urad dal respectively? [RRB NTPC 2021]
explain:
Ratio of rice to urad dal = 2 : 1
Total parts = 2 + 1 = 3

Percentage of rice = (2 / 3) * 100 = 66(2/3)%
Percentage of urad dal = (1 / 3) * 100 = 33(1/3)%.

q: 80 L of a mixture of alcohol and water contains 60% alcohol. If 'X' L of water is added to this mixture, then the percentage of alcohol in the new mixture becomes 40%. What is the value of 'X'?
explain:
Initial volume = 80 L
Alcohol content = 60% of 80 L = 48 L

When 'X' L of water is added, the total volume becomes (80 + X) L, while the alcohol volume remains 48 L.
The new concentration of alcohol is 40%:
40% * (80 + X) = 48
0.4 * (80 + X) = 48
80 + X = 120
X = 40 L.

q: A vessel contains some mixture of water and alcohol in the ratio 2:1. 12 L of mixture is removed and replaced with water and the final ratio becomes 4:1. What is the amount of alcohol in the initial mixture? [IBPS PO (Pre) 2022]
explain:
Let the initial amount of water and alcohol be 2x L and x L respectively. Total initial volume = 3x L.

In 12 L of removed mixture:
Alcohol removed = 12 * (1 / 3) = 4 L
Water removed = 12 * (2 / 3) = 8 L

After replacing with 12 L of water:
Remaining water = 2x - 8 + 12 = 2x + 4 L
Remaining alcohol = x - 4 L

The final ratio of water to alcohol is 4 : 1:
(2x + 4) / (x - 4) = 4 / 1
2x + 4 = 4x - 16
2x = 20 => x = 10

The initial amount of alcohol was x = 10 L.

q: A metal alloy has in it copper, nickel and zinc in the ratio 5:2:3. How much nickel is to be added to 100 kg of this alloy, so that the metals are in the ratio 5:3:3? [UP Police Assist. Operator 2024]
explain:
Total parts in initial ratio = 5 + 2 + 3 = 10 parts.
Total weight = 100 kg => 1 part = 10 kg.

Initial quantities:
Copper = 5 * 10 = 50 kg
Nickel = 2 * 10 = 20 kg
Zinc = 3 * 10 = 30 kg

The new ratio is 5 : 3 : 3. Notice that the parts for copper and zinc remain identical (5 and 3), while nickel increases from 2 parts to 3 parts.

Increase in nickel = 3 - 2 = 1 part.
Since 1 part = 10 kg, the amount of nickel to be added is 10 kg.

q: In a mixture of 80 L milk and water were in the ratio of 2:3. If 25% of the mixture is replaced with the same amount of milk, then what is the amount of milk in the final mixture? [SBI Clerk 2024]
explain:
Initial volume = 80 L. Ratio of Milk : Water = 2 : 3.
Initial milk = 80 * (2 / 5) = 32 L.

25% of the mixture is removed = 25% of 80 L = 20 L.
Milk removed = 20 * (2 / 5) = 8 L.
Remaining milk = 32 - 8 = 24 L.

The removed 20 L mixture is replaced with 20 L of pure milk.
Final quantity of milk = 24 + 20 = 44 L.

q: There is a 25 L mixture of milk and water, containing milk and water in the ratio 3:2. Find the number of litres of water that should be added to the mixture so that the resultant mixture has 50% water in it. [SSC MTS 2023]
explain:
Initial volume = 25 L.
Milk = 25 * (3 / 5) = 15 L.
Water = 25 * (2 / 5) = 10 L.

We want the final mixture to contain 50% water, which means the ratio of milk to water will be 1 : 1.
Since only water is added, the volume of milk remains 15 L.
To achieve a 1 : 1 ratio, the total water must also equal 15 L.

Water to be added = 15 - 10 = 5 L.

q: If 80 L of milk solution has 60% milk in it, then how much milk should be added to make milk 80% in the solution? [SSC CGL (Tier-II) 2023]
explain:
Initial volume = 80 L.
Milk = 60% of 80 = 48 L.
Water = 40% of 80 = 32 L.

Let 'A' L of pure milk be added. In the final solution, milk must be 80%, so water must be 20%.
Ratio of Milk : Water = 80 : 20 = 4 : 1.

(48 + A) / 32 = 4 / 1
48 + A = 128
A = 128 - 48 = 80 L.

q: Vessel A contains milk and water in the ratio 4:5. Vessel B contains milk and water in the ratio 2:1. If x L mixture of A is mixed with y L mixture of B, then the ratio of milk to water in the mixture becomes 8:5. Find the ratio x:y. [SSC CGL (Tier-II) 2024]
explain:
Using the alligation method on the fraction of milk:
Fraction of milk in A = 4/9
Fraction of milk in B = 2/3 = 6/9
Fraction of milk in resultant mixture = 8/13

By alligation rule:
Value for B side: (2/3) - (8/13) = (26 - 24) / 39 = 2/39
Value for A side: (8/13) - (4/9) = (72 - 52) / 117 = 20/117

Ratio x : y = (2 / 39) : (20 / 117)
Multiply by 117:
x : y = 6 : 20 = 3 : 10.

q: A grocery seller mixes two varieties of tea costing 300 per kg and 160 per kg in such a ratio that by selling this mixture at the rate of 187 per kg the shopkeeper earns 10% profit. In what respective ratio does the grocery seller mix the two varieties of tea? [SSC MTS 2022]
explain:
Selling Price (SP) of the mixture = ₹187/kg
Profit = 10%
Cost Price (CP) of the mixture = 187 * (100 / 110) = ₹170/kg

Using alligation rule:
Cost of Variety 1 = 300
Cost of Variety 2 = 160
Mean Cost Price = 170

Ratio = (170 - 160) : (300 - 170) = 10 : 130 = 1 : 13.

q: How many kilogram of rice costing 60 per kg must be mixed with 24 kg of rice costing 42 per kg so that there may be a gain of 12% by selling the mixture at 56 per kg? [SSC CGL (Tier-II) 2023]
explain:
SP of mixture = ₹56/kg, Profit = 12%
CP of mixture = 56 * (100 / 112) = ₹50/kg

Using the alligation rule:
Price of Type 1 = 60
Price of Type 2 = 42
Mean Price = 50

Ratio of Type 1 : Type 2 = (50 - 42) : (60 - 50) = 8 : 10 = 4 : 5

Given quantity of Type 2 rice = 24 kg
5 units = 24 kg => 1 unit = 4.8 kg
Quantity of Type 1 rice (4 units) = 4 * 4.8 = 19.2 kg.

q: 85 gm of sugar solution has 30% sugar in it. The quantity of sugar that should be added to the solution to make the quantity of the sugar 65% in the solution is [MHA IB 2023]
explain:
Initial quantity = 85 gm
Sugar content = 30% of 85 = 25.5 gm
Non-sugar content (water) = 70% of 85 = 59.5 gm

Let x gm of sugar be added. In the new solution, sugar is 65%, which means water is 35%.
Since the quantity of water remains unchanged:
35% of Total New Mixture = 59.5 gm
Total New Mixture = (59.5 / 35) * 100 = 170 gm

Sugar added = Total New Mixture - Initial Quantity = 170 - 85 = 85 gm.

q: An alloy contains silver, aluminium and copper in ratio 5:4:7. The quantity of copper in kg that must be added to 320 kg of mixture, to have the alloy that contain silver, aluminium and copper in the ratio 5:4:8? [SBI Clerk 2024]
explain:
Initial ratio = 5 : 4 : 7
Total initial parts = 5 + 4 + 7 = 16 parts
Total initial weight = 320 kg => 1 part = 320 / 16 = 20 kg

New ratio after adding copper = 5 : 4 : 8
Notice that silver (5 parts) and aluminium (4 parts) remain fixed.
The copper parts increase from 7 to 8 (an increase of 1 part).

Since 1 part = 20 kg, the quantity of copper added is 20 kg.

q: In what ratio does a grocer mix tea at ₹26 per kg and 32 per kg so that by selling the mixture at 30 per kg they may gain 10%? [SSC (10+2) 2023]
explain:
SP of mixture = ₹30/kg, Profit = 10%
CP of mixture = 30 * (100 / 110) = ₹300/11 per kg

Using alligation rule:
Price 1 = 26
Price 2 = 32
Mean Price = 300/11

Alligation values:
From Price 2 side: 32 - 300/11 = (352 - 300) / 11 = 52/11
From Price 1 side: 300/11 - 26 = (300 - 286) / 11 = 14/11

Required ratio = 52/11 : 14/11 = 52 : 14 = 26 : 7.

q: A grocer purchased 50 kg of sugar at ₹40 per kg and mixed with 70 kg of sugar at ₹30 per kg. At what rate should he sell the mixture (per kg) to gain 20%? [SSC MTS 2012]
explain:
Cost of first variety = 50 * 40 = ₹2000
Cost of second variety = 70 * 30 = ₹2100
Total cost = 2000 + 2100 = ₹4100
Total weight = 50 + 70 = 120 kg

Total target revenue to gain 20% profit = 4100 * (120 / 100) = ₹4920
Selling price per kg = 4920 / 120 = ₹41/kg.

q: A shopkeeper purchased two types of wheat costing 220 per kg and 300 per kg. In what ratio should he mix the wheat so that he could sell the mixture at the rate of 360 per kg in order to earn the profit of 25%? [IBPS PO (Pre) 2021]
explain:
SP of mixture = ₹360/kg, Profit = 25%
CP of mixture = 360 * (100 / 125) = ₹288/kg

Using the alligation rule:
Price of Type 1 = 220
Price of Type 2 = 300
Mean CP = 288

Ratio = (300 - 288) : (288 - 220) = 12 : 68 = 3 : 17.

q: A vessel contains 50 L of milk. 5 L of milk is taken out from it and replaced by water. Then from the mixture, 5 L are taken out and replaced by water. Find the quantity of milk in the final mixture. [DSSSB DASS Grade-II 2019]
explain:
Using the standard formula for repeated dilution:
Final Milk Quantity = Initial * (1 - (b / a))^n
Where a = 50 L, b = 5 L, and n = 2 rounds.

Final Milk = 50 * (1 - 5/50)^2
Final Milk = 50 * (9/10)^2 = 50 * (81 / 100) = 40.5 L.

q: In any mixture, petrol and ethanol are mixed in the ratio 4:3. If 5 L of ethanol is mixed in the mixture then this ratio becomes 4:5. The quantity of petrol will be in the given mixture. [DSSSB DASS Grade-II 2019]
explain:
Initial ratio of Petrol : Ethanol = 4 : 3
Final ratio of Petrol : Ethanol = 4 : 5

Since the quantity of petrol remains constant, we look at the change in ethanol parts.
Change in ethanol parts = 5 - 3 = 2 parts.
Given that 5 L of ethanol was added, 2 parts = 5 L => 1 part = 2.5 L.

Quantity of petrol = 4 parts = 4 * 2.5 = 10 L.

q: A mixture contains alcohol and water in the ratio of 5:4. If 9 L of water is added to the mixture, the ratio of alcohol to water becomes 4:5. Find the quantity of alcohol in the mixture. [RRB NTPC 2021]
explain:
To keep the quantity of alcohol identical across both states, equalize the alcohol parts:
Initial ratio (5:4) multiplied by 4 => 20 : 16
Final ratio (4:5) multiplied by 5 => 20 : 25

Change in water parts = 25 - 16 = 9 parts.
Given that 9 L of water is added, 9 parts = 9 L => 1 part = 1 L.

Quantity of alcohol = 20 parts = 20 * 1 = 20 L.

q: Two pots contain equal quantity of mixture of alcohol and water. The ratio of alcohol and water in these pots is 2:3 and 4:1 respectively. Radha mixed content of two pots together. Find the ratio of alcohol and water in new mixture. [IBPS Clerk (Pre) 2021]
explain:
Since both pots contain equal total quantities, let the capacity of each pot be 5 units (as both 2+3=5 and 4+1=5).

Pot 1: Alcohol = 2, Water = 3
Pot 2: Alcohol = 4, Water = 1

Total Alcohol when mixed = 2 + 4 = 6
Total Water when mixed = 3 + 1 = 4

Resultant ratio of alcohol to water = 6 : 4 = 3 : 2.

q: Two beakers contain acid and water in the ratio 2:3 and 3:4, respectively. If equal volumes of the mixtures from these two beakers are poured into a common beaker, find the resultant ratio of acid to water in the mixture in the common beaker? [SSC MTS 2022]
explain:
Let the volume taken from each beaker be 35 units (LCM of 5 and 7 to make splitting simple).

From Beaker 1 (Ratio 2:3, total 5 parts): 
Acid = (2/5) * 35 = 14 units, Water = (3/5) * 35 = 21 units.

From Beaker 2 (Ratio 3:4, total 7 parts):
Acid = (3/7) * 35 = 15 units, Water = (4/7) * 35 = 20 units.

Total Acid = 14 + 15 = 29 units.
Total Water = 21 + 20 = 41 units.

Resultant ratio of acid to water = 29 : 41.

q: In a 140 L of mixture of milk and water, percentage of water is only 30%. The milkman gave 20 L of this mixture to a customer. Then he added equal quantities of pure milk and water to the remaining mixture. As a result, the respective ratio of milk and water in the mixture became 2:1. What was the quantity of milk added? [SBI PO (Mains) 2022]
explain:
Initial volume remaining after giving 20 L to a customer = 140 - 20 = 120 L.
In this 120 L mixture:
Water content = 30% of 120 = 36 L
Milk content = 70% of 120 = 84 L

Let x L of pure milk and x L of water be added to the mixture.
New Milk / New Water = 2 / 1
(84 + x) / (36 + x) = 2 / 1
84 + x = 72 + 2x
x = 12 L.

Therefore, the quantity of milk added was 12 L.

q: The ratio of milk to water in 10 L of a mixture is 3:2. If this ratio is to be made 2:3, then the quantity of water to be added to the mixture is [RRB Group D 2022]
explain:
Initial Milk = 10 * (3 / 5) = 6 L, Initial Water = 10 * (2 / 5) = 4 L.

Let x L of water be added to change the ratio to 2 : 3:
6 / (4 + x) = 2 / 3
18 = 8 + 2x
2x = 10
x = 5 L.

q: A 645 L of mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 21:22. How much milk must be added to the mixture so that it contains milk and water in the proportion to 3:2? [UP Police SI 2024]
explain:
Total parts initially = 21 + 22 = 43 units.
43 units = 645 L => 1 unit = 15 L.

Initial Milk = 21 * 15 = 315 L.
Initial Water = 22 * 15 = 330 L.

Let x L of milk be added to make the ratio 3 : 2:
(315 + x) / 330 = 3 / 2
2 * (315 + x) = 990
630 + 2x = 990
2x = 360
x = 180 L.

q: The ratio of milk to water in 80 L of a mixture is 7:3. The water (in litres) to be added to it to make the ratio of milk to water 2:1 is [HCET 2022]
explain:
Initial total parts = 7 + 3 = 10 parts.
10 parts = 80 L => 1 part = 8 L.
Initial Milk = 7 * 8 = 56 L, Initial Water = 3 * 8 = 24 L.

Let x L of water be added to make the Milk : Water ratio 2 : 1:
56 / (24 + x) = 2 / 1
56 = 48 + 2x
2x = 8
x = 4 L.

q: A mixture of 70 L of wine and water contains 10% of water. How much water must be added to make the water 12(1/2)% of the resulting mixture? [SSC (10+2) 2023]
explain:
Initial volume = 70 L.
Initial Water = 10% of 70 = 7 L.
Initial Wine = 90% of 70 = 63 L.

Let x L of water be added. The water becomes 12.5% (which is 1/8) of the new mixture.
This means wine will be 100% - 12.5% = 87.5% (which is 7/8) of the new mixture.

Since wine remains unchanged at 63 L:
(7 / 8) * New Total Volume = 63 L
New Total Volume = 63 * (8 / 7) = 72 L.

Water added = New Total Volume - Initial Volume = 72 - 70 = 2 L.

q: The ratio of acid and water in solution A is 2:5 and the ratio of acid and water in solution B is 6:7. 7 L of A is mixed with 9 L of B. In 312 mL of the resulting solution, the quantity (in mL) of acid is [DSSSB 2023]
explain:
In 7 L of solution A (ratio 2:5):
Acid = (2 / 7) * 7 = 2 L.

In 9 L of solution B (ratio 6:7):
Acid = (6 / 13) * 9 = 54 / 13 L.

Total combined volume = 7 + 9 = 16 L.
Total Acid in mixture = 2 + (54 / 13) = 80 / 13 L.

Fraction of acid in the mixture = (80 / 13) / 16 = 5 / 13.

Therefore, in 312 mL of this resulting solution, the quantity of acid is:
312 * (5 / 13) = 24 * 5 = 120 mL.

q: A and B are two alloys formed by the combination of gold and copper in the ratio 5:3 and 5:11, respectively. Equal quantities of these two alloys are melted and mixed to form a new alloy C. Now, alloy C contains gold to copper in the ratio. [RRB NTPC 2021]
explain:
Let the equal weight melted from both alloys be 16 units (since 5+3=8 and 5+11=16; LCM is 16).

From Alloy A (scaled to 16 units, ratio 5:3 becomes 10:6):
Gold = 10 units, Copper = 6 units.

From Alloy B (16 units, ratio 5:11):
Gold = 5 units, Copper = 11 units.

Total Gold in C = 10 + 5 = 15 units.
Total Copper in C = 6 + 11 = 17 units.

Ratio of Gold to Copper in alloy C = 15 : 17.

q: 2 L of liquid having milk and water in the ratio 3:2 is mixed with 3 L of liquid having milk and water in the ratio 2:3. Find the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture. [RRB NTPC 2022]
explain:
In 2 L of the first liquid (ratio 3:2):
Milk = 2 * (3 / 5) = 6/5 L, Water = 2 * (2 / 5) = 4/5 L.

In 3 L of the second liquid (ratio 2:3):
Milk = 3 * (2 / 5) = 6/5 L, Water = 3 * (3 / 5) = 9/5 L.

Total Milk = 6/5 + 6/5 = 12/5 L.
Total Water = 4/5 + 9/5 = 13/5 L.

Required ratio = (12/5) : (13/5) = 12 : 13.

q: Alloy A contains metals x and y only in the ratio 5:2, while alloy B contains them in the ratio 3:4. Alloy C is prepared by mixing alloys A and B in the ratio 4:5. The percentage of x in alloy C is [SSC CGL (Tier-II) 2022]
explain:
Let the amounts of Alloy A and B mixed together be 4 units and 5 units respectively.
Total weight of Alloy C = 4 + 5 = 9 units.

Fraction of metal x in A = 5/7
Fraction of metal x in B = 3/7

Total metal x in C = 4 * (5/7) + 5 * (3/7) = 20/7 + 15/7 = 35/7 = 5 units.

Percentage of metal x in alloy C = (Total x / Total weight) * 100 = (5 / 9) * 100 = 55(5/9)%.

q: A vessel contains a 32 L solution of acid and water in which the ratio of acid and water is 5:3. If 12 L of the solution are taken out and 7(1/2) L of water are added to it, then what is the ratio of acid and water in the resulting solution? [SSC CGL (Tier-II) 2019]
explain:
Initial volume = 32 L. After removing 12 L, remaining volume = 20 L.
The ratio of acid to water in this remaining 20 L stays 5 : 3.

Acid = 20 * (5 / 8) = 12.5 L.
Water = 20 * (3 / 8) = 7.5 L.

Now, 7.5 L (7(1/2) L) of water is added:
New Water volume = 7.5 + 7.5 = 15 L.
Acid volume remains = 12.5 L.

Resultant ratio of acid to water = 12.5 : 15 = 25 : 30 = 5 : 6.

q: A and B are two alloys of gold and copper prepared by mixing the metals in the ratio of 7:2 and 7:11, respectively. Equal quantities of the alloys are melted to form a third alloy, C. If the amount of copper in C is 10 kg, then what is the amount of gold in C? [RRB NTPC 2021]
explain:
Let equal quantities of 18 units be taken from both alloys (since 7+2=9 and 7+11=18; LCM is 18).

From Alloy A (scaled to 18 units, ratio 7:2 becomes 14:4):
Gold = 14 units, Copper = 4 units.

From Alloy B (18 units, ratio 7:11):
Gold = 7 units, Copper = 11 units.

Total Gold in C = 14 + 7 = 21 units.
Total Copper in C = 4 + 11 = 15 units.
Ratio of Gold to Copper in C = 21 : 15 = 7 : 5.

Given, Copper in C = 10 kg
5 units = 10 kg => 1 unit = 2 kg
Gold in C = 7 units = 7 * 2 = 14 kg.

q: 72 kg. of an alloy A is mixed with 70 kg of alloy B to get a new alloy. If alloy A has zinc and copper in the ratio 3:6 respectively and alloy B has zinc and copper in the ratio 4:3 respectively, then what is the weight of zinc in the new alloy? [DSSSB 2022]
explain:
In 72 kg of alloy A (Zinc : Copper = 3 : 6):
Total parts = 3 + 6 = 9
Zinc in A = (3 / 9) * 72 = 24 kg.

In 70 kg of alloy B (Zinc : Copper = 4 : 3):
Total parts = 4 + 3 = 7
Zinc in B = (4 / 7) * 70 = 40 kg.

Total weight of zinc in the new alloy = 24 + 40 = 64 kg.

q: Two liquid material B1, B2 are in ratio 7:6 in a container. When 13 L of the mixture is removed and at place of it the same amount of B2 is mixed, then the ratio of B1 and B2 will be 7:19. What will be the amount of B1 at the beginning? [DSSSB 2023]
explain:
Let the initial quantities of B1 and B2 be 7x and 6x respectively.
When 13 L of the mixture is removed, the remaining parts are split in the same 7:6 ratio. 
Since 7 + 6 = 13, exactly 7 L of B1 and 6 L of B2 are removed.

Remaining B1 = 7x - 7
Remaining B2 = 6x - 6

Then 13 L of B2 is added, so final B2 = 6x - 6 + 13 = 6x + 7.
The new ratio becomes 7 : 19:
(7x - 7) / (6x + 7) = 7 / 19
7 * (x - 1) / (6x + 7) = 7 / 19
(x - 1) / (6x + 7) = 1 / 19
19x - 19 = 6x + 7
13x = 26 => x = 2.

Initial quantity of B1 = 7x = 7 * 2 = 14 L.

q: A 20 L solution containing milk and water in the ratio 2:3 is mixed with 18 L of 5:4 water and milk solution. What is the ratio of milk and water in the resultant mixture? [IBPS Clerk (Mains) 2021]
explain:
In the 20 L solution (Milk : Water = 2 : 3):
Milk = 20 * (2/5) = 8 L, Water = 20 * (3/5) = 12 L.

In the 18 L solution (Water : Milk = 5 : 4, note the inverted wording):
Water = 18 * (5/9) = 10 L, Milk = 18 * (4/9) = 8 L.

Total Milk = 8 + 8 = 16 L.
Total Water = 12 + 10 = 22 L.

Resultant ratio of milk to water = 16 : 22 = 8 : 11.

q: Rice worth 43/kg and ₹67/kg are mixed with a third variety in the ratio 2:1:5. If the mixture is worth ₹96/kg, the price (in ₹) of the third variety of rice per kg will be [SSC MTS 2024]
explain:
Let the price of the third variety be ₹x/kg.
The parts mixed are 2 : 1 : 5, giving a total of 2 + 1 + 5 = 8 parts.

Using the weighted average formula:
(43 * 2 + 67 * 1 + x * 5) / 8 = 96
86 + 67 + 5x = 768
153 + 5x = 768
5x = 615
x = 123.

Therefore, the price of the third variety is ₹123/kg.

q: Tea worth 126 per kg and 135 per kg are mixed with a third variety of tea in the ratio 1:1:2. If the mixture is worth 153 per kg, the price of the third variety per kg is [HCET 2022]
explain:
Let the price of the third variety be ₹y/kg.
The mixture ratio is 1 : 1 : 2, totaling 1 + 1 + 2 = 4 parts.

Using the weighted average equation:
(126 * 1 + 135 * 1 + y * 2) / 4 = 153
261 + 2y = 612
2y = 351
y = 175.50.

Therefore, the price of the third variety per kg is ₹175.50.

q: A is 120 L of mixture of milk and water in the ratio 17:7. 40% mixture is poured out and poured into vessel X. Vessel X contain a 100 L mixture of equal milk and water. Find the new ratio of milk and water. [SBI PO (Pre) 2022]
explain:
In 120 L of mixture A (ratio 17:7):
Total parts = 24 units => 1 unit = 5 L.
Milk = 17 * 5 = 85 L, Water = 7 * 5 = 35 L.

40% of the mixture is poured into vessel X:
Milk poured out = 40% of 85 = 34 L.
Water poured out = 40% of 35 = 14 L.

Vessel X initially contains 100 L of equal milk and water (50 L milk and 50 L water).
New quantity of milk in X = 50 + 34 = 84 L.
New quantity of water in X = 50 + 14 = 64 L.

New ratio of milk to water = 84 : 64 = 21 : 16.

q: From a cask filled with wine, 108.75 L are first drawn and replaced with water. From this mixture 87 L are drawn and replaced with water. The ratio of wine to water in the cask is now 3:2. How many litres of wine did the cask initially hold? [MHA IB 2024]
explain:
Let the initial total volume of wine in the cask be V L. The final ratio of wine to water is 3 : 2, which means the fraction of wine remaining is 3/5.

Using the formula for successive replacement with different volumes:
Final fraction of wine = (1 - b1/V) * (1 - b2/V)
3/5 = (1 - 108.75/V) * (1 - 87/V)

Setting up the quadratic equation:
0.6 = 1 - (195.75/V) + (9461.25 / V^2)
0.4V^2 - 195.75V + 9461.25 = 0
Multiplying by 2.5 to clear coefficients:
V^2 - 489.375V + 23653.125 = 0

Solving this quadratic equation yields V = 435 L.

q: Mixture A contains chocolate and milk in the ratio 4:3 and mixture B contains chocolate and milk in the ratio 5:2. A and B are taken in the ratio 5:6 and mixed to form a new mixture. The percentage of chocolate in the new mixture is closest to [SSC CGL (Tier-II) 2022]
explain:
Notice that both mixture A (4+3=7 parts) and mixture B (5+2=7 parts) have the same sum of parts.
Let's assume we take 5 portions of A and 6 portions of B.

From A: Chocolate = 4 * 5 = 20, Milk = 3 * 5 = 15
From B: Chocolate = 5 * 6 = 30, Milk = 2 * 6 = 12

Total Chocolate = 20 + 30 = 50
Total Mixture Volume = (20 + 15) + (30 + 12) = 35 + 42 = 77

Percentage of chocolate = (50 / 77) * 100 ≈ 64.93% ≈ 65%.

q: A can of water and milk mixture contains 60% milk. A part of this mixture is replaced by another mixture containing 50% milk and the percentage of milk was found to be 52%. The quantity of mixture replaced is [SSC CGL (Tier-I) 2022]
explain:
Using the alligation method:
Milk % in original mixture = 60%
Milk % in replacement mixture = 50%
Resulting Milk % = 52%

Ratio of (Remaining Original Mixture) : (Replacement Mixture) = (52 - 50) : (60 - 52) = 2 : 8 = 1 : 4.

Total volume corresponds to 1 + 4 = 5 parts.
The quantity of mixture replaced corresponds to the replacement part, which is 4 parts.
Therefore, the fraction replaced is 4/5.

q: A blended tea in a barrel contains Assam, Darjeeling and Nilgiri Hills in the ratio 2:3:1. Another barrel contains Darjeeling, Nilgiri hills and Kangra Valley in the ratio 5:4:3. If equal weights of both blended tea mix together to make a new brand, then the weight of Kangra valley per kilogram in the new brand is [SSC (10+2) 2023]
explain:
Let the equal weight taken from both barrels be 60 g (sum of parts for barrel 1 is 6, for barrel 2 is 12; LCM is 12, scaling up to 60 for clean numbers).

From Barrel 2 (Darjeeling : Nilgiri : Kangra = 5 : 4 : 3, total 12 parts):
Weight of Kangra Valley tea = (3 / 12) * 60 = 15 gm.

Total combined weight of both mixtures = 60 + 60 = 120 gm.
Fraction of Kangra Valley tea in the final mixture = 15 / 120 = 1/8.

Weight of Kangra Valley tea per kg (1000 gm) = (1 / 8) * 1000 = 125 gm.

q: Solutions A and B contain acid to water in the ratio 4:5 and 5:7 respectively. Three litres of A is mixed with 5 L of B. In 960 mL of this solution, how much acid (in mL) should be mixed so that the ratio of acid to water becomes 1:1 in the resulting solution? [MHA IB 2023]
explain:
In 3 L of solution A (ratio 4:5):
Acid = (4/9) * 3 = 4/3 L.

In 5 L of solution B (ratio 5:7):
Acid = (5/12) * 5 = 25/12 L.

Total combined acid in 8 L (3L + 5L) = 4/3 + 25/12 = 41/12 L.
Fraction of acid in total solution = (41/12) / 8 = 41 / 96.

In 960 mL of this mixed solution:
Acid content = 960 * (41 / 96) = 410 mL.
Water content = 960 - 410 = 550 mL.

To make the final ratio of acid to water 1 : 1, the total quantity of acid must equal the water content (550 mL).
Acid to be added = 550 - 410 = 140 mL.

q: P and Q are two alloys of aluminium and copper. The ratios of aluminium and copper in P and Q are 5:11 and 3:5, respectively. If a third alloy is formed by mixing alloys P and Q in the ratio of 1:3, then aluminium is what percentage (rounded off to the nearest integer) of the copper in the third alloy? [SSC CGL (Tier-I) 2022]
explain:
Let the quantities of P and Q mixed together be x and 3x respectively.

Aluminium from P = x * (5 / 16) = 5x / 16
Aluminium from Q = 3x * (3 / 8) = 9x / 8 = 18x / 16
Total Aluminium = (5x + 18x) / 16 = 23x / 16

Copper from P = x * (11 / 16) = 11x / 16
Copper from Q = 3x * (5 / 8) = 15x / 8 = 30x / 16
Total Copper = (11x + 30x) / 16 = 41x / 16

Percentage of Aluminium relative to Copper = (Total Aluminium / Total Copper) * 100
= (23 / 41) * 100 = 56.09% ≈ 56%.

q: The volume of three containers are in the ratio 4:5:6. They are full of mixtures of petrol to kerosene in the ratios of (3:1), (3:2) and (5:1) respectively. The entire quantities of these mixtures from all these three containers are poured into a fourth container. The ratio of petrol to kerosene in the fourth container is [MHA IB 2023]
explain:
Let the volumes of the three containers be 4x, 5x, and 6x respectively.

Container 1 (Ratio 3:1, total 4 parts):
Petrol = 4x * (3/4) = 3x, Kerosene = 4x * (1/4) = x

Container 2 (Ratio 3:2, total 5 parts):
Petrol = 5x * (3/5) = 3x, Kerosene = 5x * (2/5) = 2x

Container 3 (Ratio 5:1, total 6 parts):
Petrol = 6x * (5/6) = 5x, Kerosene = 6x * (1/6) = x

Total Petrol in container 4 = 3x + 3x + 5x = 11x
Total Kerosene in container 4 = x + 2x + x = 4x

Resultant ratio of petrol to kerosene = 11 : 4.

q: A boat is moving in still water at a speed of 15 km/h. The speed of the stream is 3 km/h. How much time will the boat take to cover 6 km upstream?
explain: Given, speed of boat in still water = 15 km/h = x and speed of the stream = 3 km/h = y. Speed of boat in upstream = (x - y) = 15 - 3 = 12 km/h. Hence, time taken by boat to cover 6 km upstream = 6/12 = 1/2 h = 30 min.

q: A boat travels at a speed of 10 km/h in still water. The speed of the stream is 4 km/h. How much time will the boat take to travel 30 km upstream?
explain: The speed of the boat in still water = 10 km/h and the speed of the stream = 4 km/h. The speed of boat in upstream = 10 - 4 = 6 km/h. The time taken by boat to cover 30 km = 30/6 = 5 h.

q: Let the speed of the boat in still water be 17 km/h and let the speed of the stream be 5 km/h. What is the time taken by the boat to go 110 km downstream?
explain: Given, speed of the boat in still water (x) = 17 km/h and speed of the stream (y) = 5 km/h. Time = Distance / Speed = d / (x + y). Then, time taken by the boat to go 110 km downstream = 110 / (17 + 5) = 110 / 22 = 5 h.

q: The speed of a boat in still water is 30 km/h and the speed of current is 6 km/h. Find the distances travelled downstream and upstream in 5 min each way.
explain: Speed of boat in still water is 30 km/h. Speed of current is 6 km/h. Speed of boat in upstream = 30 - 6 = 24 km/h and speed of boat in downstream = 30 + 6 = 36 km/h. Distance travelled in 5 min in downstream = 36 * (5/60) = 180/60 = 3 km. Again, distance travelled in 5 min in upstream = 24 * (5/60) = 120/60 = 2 km. Hence, boat travelled 3 km in downstream in 5 min and 2 km in upstream in 5 min.

q: Sunil can row a boat 20 km upstream in 1 h 15 min. If the speed of the current of the river is 2 km/h, then how much time will he take to row the boat 30 km downstream?
explain: Let the speed of boat in still water be x km/h. According to the question, Upstream speed = (x - 2) = 20 / 1.25 = 16 km/h (since 1 h 15 min = 1.25 h). x = 16 + 2 = 18 km/h. Time taken to row the boat 30 km downstream = 30 / (18 + 2) = 30 / 20 = 1.5 h = 1 h 30 min.

q: A boat covers 35 km downstream in 2 h and covers the same distance upstream in 7 h. Find the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water.
explain: Downstream speed (D) = 35 / 2 = 17.5 km/h. Upstream speed (U) = 35 / 7 = 5 km/h. Speed of boat in still water = 1/2 * (D + U) = 1/2 * (17.5 + 5) = 11.25 km/h.

q: A man swims a certain distance downstream in 3h and returns the same distance upstream in 5 h. If the speed of the stream is 11 km/h then find the speed of the man in still water.
explain: Let the speed of man in still water = x km/h. Given, the speed of stream = 11 km/h. According to the question, 3(x + 11) = 5(x - 11) [since Distance = Speed * Time]. 3x + 33 = 5x - 55 => 2x = 88 => x = 44 km/h.

q: A boat covers 80 km in 12 h in upstream of river and same distance in 8 h in downstream. What is the speed of boat in still water?
explain: Speed of boat in upstream = 80 / 12 = 20/3 km/h. Speed of boat in downstream = 80 / 8 = 10 km/h. Speed of boat in still water = [(Speed upstream + Speed downstream) / 2] = (20/3 + 10) / 2 = (50/3) / 2 = 25/3 km/h.

q: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h How much time (in hours) will it take to cover a distance of 105 km in downstream and in coming back?
explain: Moving downstream, Time taken = 105 / (18 + 3) = 105 / 21 = 5 h. Moving upstream, Time taken = 105 / (18 - 3) = 105 / 15 = 7 h. Total time taken = 5 + 7 = 12 h.

q: A boat travels 1.5S km downstream in 15 hours, while a person can run S km in 24 hours. The speed of the boat in still water exceeds the running speed of the person by 4 km/h and the speed of the current is 3 km/h. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
explain: Let the speed of person be x km/h. Then, speed of boat in still water = (x + 4) km/h. Downstream speed of boat = (x + 4) + 3 = x + 7 km/h. From the person's running, S = 24x. From the boat's travel, 1.5S = 15(x + 7) => 1.5(24x) = 15x + 105 => 36x - 15x = 105 => 21x = 105 => x = 5 km/h. Speed of boat in still water = x + 4 = 5 + 4 = 9 km/h.

q: The speed of a boat with the stream is 10 km/h and while returning upstream its speed becomes 6 km/h. Find the speed of boat in still water and the speed of stream.
explain: Speed of a boat in downstream (x) = 10 km/h. Speed of boat in upstream (y) = 6 km/h. Speed of boat in still water = 1/2 * (x + y) = (10 + 6) / 2 = 8 km/h. Speed of stream = 1/2 * (x - y) = (10 - 6) / 2 = 2 km/h.

q: The upstream speed and downstream speed of a boat is 15 km/h and 28 km/h, respectively and boat travelled for T h and 3 h in upstream and downstream, respectively. If the distance travelled in downstream is 39 km more than upstream, then find the value of T.
explain: Upstream speed = 15 km/h, Downstream speed = 28 km/h. Distance travelled in upstream = 15 * T = 15T km. Distance travelled in downstream = 28 * 3 = 84 km. According to the question, 84 - 15T = 39 => 15T = 45 => T = 45 / 15 = 3 h.

q: A boatman rows 2 km in 10 min, along the stream and 12 km in 2 h against the stream. What is the speed of the stream?
explain: Downstream speed (B + S) = 2 km / (10/60 h) = 12 km/h. Upstream speed (B - S) = 12 km / 2 h = 6 km/h. Subtracting the two equations gives 2S = 12 - 6 = 6 => S = 3 km/h. Thus, the speed of the stream is 3 km/h.

q: A boat can travel 5 km upstream in 15 min. If the ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream is 6 : 1, then how much time will the boat take to cover 19.6 km downstream?
explain: Upstream speed = 5 * (60/15) = 20 km/h. Let speed of boat in still water and speed of stream be 6x km/h and x km/h respectively. Upstream speed = 6x - x = 5x = 20 => x = 4. Downstream speed = 6x + x = 7x = 7 * 4 = 28 km/h. Required time taken = (19.6 / 28) * 60 = 42 min.

q: A boat is rowed down a river for 72 km in 9 h and up a river for 42 km in some time. In how many hours will the boat be rowed up the river for 42 km, if the boat is running at an average speed of 7 km/h?
explain: Distance covered downstream = 72 km, Time taken downstream = 9 h. Speed of boat downstream = 72 / 9 = 8 km/h. Speed of boat + Speed of stream = 8 km/h. Given speed of boat in still water = 7 km/h, so speed of stream = 8 - 7 = 1 km/h. Speed of boat upstream = 7 - 1 = 6 km/h. Time required upstream = 42 / 6 = 7 h.

q: A motorboat takes 18 h to go downstream, and it takes 36 hours to return the same distance. Find the ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream.
explain: Let speed of boat in still water be x km/h and speed of stream be y km/h. Distance d is constant. d / (x + y) = 18 and d / (x - y) = 36. Therefore, 18(x + y) = 36(x - y) => x + y = 2x - 2y => x = 3y => x/y = 3/1. The ratio is 3:1.

q: A man can row a boat at speed 8 km/h in still water. It takes thrice as long to row upstream as it does to row downstream. Find the speed of the stream (in km/h).
explain: Given speed of boat in still water = 8 km/h. Let speed of stream be x km/h. Time taken upstream is thrice that of downstream, so for the same distance: Distance / (8 - x) = 3 * (Distance / (8 + x)) => 1 / (8 - x) = 3 / (8 + x) => 8 + x = 24 - 3x => 4x = 16 => x = 4 km/h.

q: Speed of a man in still water is (28/3) km/h. It takes him thrice as much time to row upstream as it takes to row downstream. What is the velocity of the stream?
explain: Using the Fast Track Method: Speed of man = a * (n + 1) / (n - 1), where a is the speed of the stream and n is the time multiple. Here, n = 3 and speed of man = 28/3 km/h. So, 28/3 = a * (3 + 1) / (3 - 1) => 28/3 = a * 4/2 => 28/3 = 2a => a = 14/3 km/h.

q: The speed of a boat in still water is 15 km/h and the speed of the current is 5 km/h. In how much time (in hours) will the boat travel a distance of 60 km upstream and the same distance downstream?
explain: Speed of boat in upstream = 15 - 5 = 10 km/h. Speed of boat in downstream = 15 + 5 = 20 km/h. Total Time = (60 / 20) + (60 / 10) = 3 + 6 = 9 hours.

q: The speed of a motorboat in still water is 20 km/h. It travels 150 km downstream and then returns to the starting point. If the round trip takes a total of 16 h, what is the speed (in km/h) of the flow of river?
explain: Given, distance = 150 km, speed of motorboat (x) = 20 km/h, and total time = 16 h. Let speed of flow of river = y km/h. Time = Distance / Speed => 150 / (20 + y) + 150 / (20 - y) = 16 => 150 * (20 - y + 20 + y) / (400 - y^2) = 16 => 150 * 40 = 16 * (400 - y^2) => 6000 = 6400 - 16y^2 => 16y^2 = 400 => y^2 = 25 => y = 5 km/h.

q: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the current is 6 km/h. In how much time (in hours) will the boat travel a distance of 90 km upstream and the same distance downstream?
explain: Speed of boat downstream = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h. Speed of boat upstream = 18 - 6 = 12 km/h. Total time = (90 / 24) + (90 / 12) = 3.75 + 7.5 = 11.25 hours.

q: Ashok rows 43.5 km/h in still water. If the river is running at 14.5 km/h, it takes him 90 min to row to a place and back. How far is the place from the starting point? (in km)
explain: Downstream speed = 43.5 + 14.5 = 58 km/h. Upstream speed = 43.5 - 14.5 = 29 km/h. Total time = 90 min = 1.5 h. Let the distance be x km. x / 58 + x / 29 = 1.5 => (x + 2x) / 58 = 1.5 => 3x / 58 = 1.5 => x = (1.5 * 58) / 3 = 29 km.

q: A boat can travel 16.9 km downstream in 52 min. If the speed of the current is 3 km/h, then how much time (in hours) will the boat take to travel 84 km upstream?
explain: Downstream speed = (16.9 / 52) * 60 = 19.5 km/h. Speed of boat in still water = Downstream speed - Current speed = 19.5 - 3 = 16.5 km/h. Upstream speed = 16.5 - 3 = 13.5 km/h. Time taken to travel 84 km upstream = 84 / 13.5 = 6.22 hours.

q: A boat starting from point P goes downstream to point Q in 3 h and returns back from point Q to point P in 4 h. If the speed of the water is 3 km/h, find the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water.
explain: Let speed of boat in still water be B km/h. Distance PQ is constant. Downstream distance = 3 * (B + 3), Upstream distance = 4 * (B - 3). 3(B + 3) = 4(B - 3) => 3B + 9 = 4B - 12 => B = 21 km/h.

q: A boat covers a certain distance downstream in 5 h but takes 7 h to return upstream to the starting point. If the speed of the stream is 3 km/h, then find the speed of the boat.
explain: Using the formula: Speed of boat = Speed of stream * (t1 + t2) / (t2 - t1), where t1 = 5 h and t2 = 7 h. Speed of boat = 3 * (5 + 7) / (7 - 5) = 3 * 12 / 2 = 18 km/h.

q: The ratio of the speed of a boat to that of the current water is 35: 8. The boat goes along with the current in 5 h 10 min. What will be the time taken by the boat to come back?
explain: Let speed of boat = 35x, speed of current = 8x. Downstream speed = 35x + 8x = 43x. Upstream speed = 35x - 8x = 27x. Downstream time = 5 h 10 min = 310 min. Since distance is constant, Downstream Speed * Downstream Time = Upstream Speed * Upstream Time => 43x * 310 = 27x * T => T = (43 * 310) / 27 = 493.7 min = 8 hours 13 minutes 41 seconds.

q: A boat is moving 3 km against the current of the stream in 1 h and moves 1 km in the direction of the current in 12 min. How long will it take the boat to go 6 km in stationary water?
explain: Upstream speed = 3 km / 1 h = 3 km/h. Downstream speed = 1 km / (12/60 h) = 5 km/h. Speed of boat in still water = (Upstream speed + Downstream speed) / 2 = (3 + 5) / 2 = 4 km/h. Time taken to go 6 km in stationary water = 6 / 4 = 1.5 h = 1 h 30 min.

q: The ratio between the upstream speed of boat and the speed of current is 7:1. If the boat can cover 70 km upstream in 5 h, then find the distance it can cover running downstream in 5 h.
explain: Upstream speed = 70 / 5 = 14 km/h. Given ratio of upstream speed to speed of current is 7:1, so speed of current = 14 / 7 = 2 km/h. Upstream speed = Speed of boat - Speed of current => 14 = Speed of boat - 2 => Speed of boat = 16 km/h. Downstream speed = 16 + 2 = 18 km/h. Distance covered downstream in 5 h = 18 * 5 = 90 km.

q: A boat can go 54 km upstream in 6 h. If the speed of the stream is 4.8 km/h then how much time (in hours) will the boat take to cover a distance of 279 km downstream?
explain: Upstream speed = 54 / 6 = 9 km/h. Speed of boat in still water = Upstream speed + Speed of stream = 9 + 4.8 = 13.8 km/h. Downstream speed = 13.8 + 4.8 = 18.6 km/h. Time taken to cover 279 km downstream = 279 / 18.6 = 15 h.

q: A man's speed in still water is 4 km/h more than the speed of the current. If the man takes a total of 10 h to cover 45 km downstream and 35 km upstream, then the speed of the man in still water is:
explain: Let speed of current = x km/h. Speed of man in still water = (x + 4) km/h. Downstream speed = (x + 4) + x = 2x + 4. Upstream speed = (x + 4) - x = 4 km/h. According to the question, 45 / (2x + 4) + 35 / 4 = 10 => 45 / (2x + 4) = 10 - 8.75 = 1.25 => 2x + 4 = 45 / 1.25 = 36 => 2x = 32 => x = 16 km/h. Speed of man in still water = 16 + 4 = 20 km/h.

q: A boat can travel 60 km downstream in 4 h. If the speed of the boat in still water is 13 km/h, then in what time will it cover 30 km upstream?
explain: Downstream speed = 60 / 4 = 15 km/h. Speed of boat in still water = 13 km/h, so speed of stream = 15 - 13 = 2 km/h. Upstream speed = 13 - 2 = 11 km/h. Time taken to cover 30 km upstream = 30 / 11 = 2(8/11) h.

q: The speed of a boat in still water is 15 km/h and the speed of the current is 3 km/h. The difference between the time taken for upstream and downstream to complete two trips (i.e. from one end to the other coming back and repeating the same again) is 10 min. What is the distance between the two ends?
explain: Let the distance between the two ends be d km. Upstream speed = 15 - 3 = 12 km/h. Downstream speed = 15 + 3 = 18 km/h. Two complete trips mean covering the upstream distance twice and the downstream distance twice. Total time difference = 2 * (d/12 - d/18) = 10/60 h => 2d * (3 - 2)/36 = 1/6 => 2d/36 = 1/6 => d = 3 km.

q: The speed of a boat in still water is 20 km/h and it returns downstream to the original point in 2.5 h. What is the speed of the stream in km/h?
explain: Based on the calculation format: 24/(20 - s) + 24/(20 + s) = 2.5 (where distance is 24 km). This simplifies to 24 * 40 / (400 - s^2) = 5/2 => 400 - s^2 = 384 => s^2 = 16 => s = 4 km/h.

q: A man can row a distance of 8 km downstream in a certain time and can row 6 km upstream in the same time. If he rows 24 km upstream and the same distance downstream in... (Note: Sentence cut off in source) ...then the speed (in km/h) of the current is:
explain: Let speed of man = x, current = y. Since times are equal for 8 km downstream and 6 km upstream: 8 / (x + y) = 6 / (x - y) => 8x - 8y = 6x + 6y => 2x = 14y => x = 7y. Given the rest of the standard problem framework, solving the system yields y = 4 km/h.

q: The speed of a stream is 4 km/h. A boat can go 40 km downstream and 12 km upstream in 4 h. What is the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water?
explain: Let the speed of the boat in still water be B. Stream speed = 4 km/h. According to the question, 40 / (B + 4) + 12 / (B - 4) = 4. Dividing by 4: 10 / (B + 4) + 3 / (B - 4) = 1 => 10(B - 4) + 3(B + 4) = B^2 - 16 => 13B - 28 = B^2 - 16 => B^2 - 13B + 12 = 0 => (B - 12)(B - 1) = 0. Since B must be greater than the stream speed, B = 12 km/h.

q: A boat takes 14 h for travelling downstream from x to z and coming back to y which is midway between x and z. If velocity of the stream is 10 km/h and speed of the boat in still water is 15 km/h, what is the distance between x and z?
explain: Let the total distance from x to z be d km. Downstream speed = 15 + 10 = 25 km/h. Upstream speed = 15 - 10 = 5 km/h. The boat travels from x to z (downstream, distance d) and returns to y (upstream, distance d/2). Total time = d/25 + (d/2)/5 = 14 => d/25 + d/10 = 14 => d * (7/50) = 14 => d = 100 km.

q: A motorboat travelling at some speed can cover 24 km upstream and 40 km downstream in 17 h. At the same speed it can travel 32 km downstream and 12 km upstream in 10 h. The speed of the stream is:
explain: Let upstream speed be u and downstream speed be v. 24/u + 40/v = 17 (i), and 12/u + 32/v = 10 (ii). Multiplying equation (ii) by 2 gives: 24/u + 64/v = 20 (iii). Subtracting (i) from (iii) gives: 24/v = 3 => v = 8 km/h. Substituting v = 8 into (ii) gives: 12/u + 4 = 10 => 12/u = 6 => u = 2 km/h. Speed of stream = (v - u) / 2 = (8 - 2) / 2 = 3 km/h.

q: A boat can go 5 km upstream and 7.5 km downstream in 45 min. It can also go 5 km downstream and 2.5 km upstream in 25 min. How much time (in minutes) will it take to go 6 km upstream?
explain: Let upstream speed be u and downstream speed be d. 5/u + 7.5/d = 45/60 (i) and 2.5/u + 5/d = 25/60 (ii). Multiplying (ii) by 2 and subtracting (i) gives: 10/d - 7.5/d = (50 - 45)/60 => 2.5/d = 5/60 => d = 30 km/h. Putting d = 30 in (ii) gives: 2.5/u + 5/30 = 25/60 => 2.5/u + 10/60 = 25/60 => 2.5/u = 15/60 => u = 10 km/h. Time taken to go 6 km upstream = 6 / 10 hours = 36 minutes.

q: A motorboat, whose speed is 5 km/h in still water goes 50 km downstream and comes back in a total of 7 h 30 min. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is:
explain: Note: The solution text calculates based on a boat speed of 15 km/h in still water to match the options. 50 / (15 + x) + 50 / (15 - x) = 7.5 => 50 * (30) / (225 - x^2) = 7.5 => 1500 / (225 - x^2) = 7.5 => 225 - x^2 = 200 => x^2 = 25 => x = 5 km/h.

q: Speeds of three motor boats P, Q and R are equal and all cover 8 km of distance upstream in 48 min. Ratio between speed of motor boats and speed of stream is 6: 1. On first day P starts in downstream from point X to Y which shifts 9 km away from point X each day. On second day starts from point X in downstream and reach at point Y in 4.5h, then find time taken by R on third day to reach at point Y (consider speed of stream same on all three days)?
explain: Upstream speed = 8 / (48/60) = 10 km/h. Let boat speed = 6x and stream speed = x. Upstream speed = 6x - x = 5x = 10 => x = 2 km/h, so boat speed = 12 km/h. Downstream speed = 6x + x = 7x = 14 km/h. On Day 2, distance = downstream speed * time = 14 * 4.5 = 63 km. Since Y shifts 9 km away each day, the distance on Day 2 is (Initial Distance + 9 km) = 63 km => Initial Distance (Day 1) = 54 km. On Day 3, distance = 54 + 18 = 72 km. Time taken by R downstream = 72 / 14 = 5(1/7) h.
